               "patch": "Index: src/research_desk/budget.py\n===================================================================\n--- src/research_desk/budget.py\t\n+++ src/research_desk/budget.py\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@\n+\"\"\"LLM call budget and usage accounting for a research run.\n+\n+The budget counts *started* LLM calls and the actual token usage reported by\n+the provider. Enforcement happens in the evidence recorder's\n+``on_chat_model_start``: once the configured call limit is reached, the next\n+call raises :class:`BudgetExhausted` so the graph aborts and no further LLM\n+request is started (NFR-003). A budget-stopped run returns incomplete research\n+and is never turned into an approvable recommendation.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import threading\n+from dataclasses import dataclass, field\n+\n+from .models import CallUsage, UsageSummary\n+\n+\n+class BudgetExhausted(Exception):\n+    \"\"\"Raised when the configured LLM call budget is exhausted.\"\"\"\n+\n+    def __init__(self, limit: int):\n+        self.limit = limit\n+        super().__init__(f\"LLM call budget exhausted (limit={limit}); refusing to start next call\")\n+\n+\n+@dataclass\n+class BudgetTracker:\n+    \"\"\"Thread-safe per-run call budget + usage accumulator.\"\"\"\n+\n+    max_calls: int | None = None\n+    _lock: threading.Lock = field(default_factory=threading.Lock, repr=False)\n+    calls_started: int = 0\n+    usage: UsageSummary = field(default_factory=UsageSummary)\n+\n+    def can_start(self) -> bool:\n+        \"\"\"Whether a new LLM call is permitted under the budget.\"\"\"\n+        if self.max_calls is None:\n+            return True\n+        return self.calls_started < self.max_calls\n+\n+    def start_call(self) -> None:\n+        \"\"\"Register the start of an LLM call; raise when budget exhausted.\"\"\"\n+        with self._lock:\n+            if not self.can_start():\n+                raise BudgetExhausted(self.max_calls)\n+            self.calls_started += 1\n+\n+    def record_usage(self, usage: CallUsage) -> None:\n+        with self._lock:\n+            self.usage.add(usage)\n+\n+    def stop_reason(self) -> str:\n+        if self.max_calls is not None and self.calls_started >= self.max_calls:\n+            return \"budget_exhausted\"\n+        return \"completed\"\n+\n+    def summary(self) -> UsageSummary:\n+        with self._lock:\n+            return UsageSummary(\n+                calls=self.calls_started,\n+                input_tokens=self.usage.input_tokens,\n+                output_tokens=self.usage.output_tokens,\n+                total_tokens=self.usage.total_tokens,\n+                stop_reason=self.stop_reason(),\n+            )\n+\n+    def merge(self, other: BudgetTracker) -> None:\n+        \"\"\"Merge another tracker's counts (used to aggregate baseline/compact arms).\"\"\"\n+        with self._lock:\n+            self.calls_started += other.calls_started\n+            self.usage.calls += other.usage.calls\n+            self.usage.input_tokens += other.usage.input_tokens\n+            self.usage.output_tokens += other.usage.output_tokens\n+            self.usage.total_tokens += other.usage.total_tokens\n",

A pack missing required material fails clearly.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import json\n+import shutil\n+import subprocess\n+import sys\n+import time\n+\n+import pytest\n+\n+from research_desk.evidence import EvidencePackError\n+from research_desk.models import LedgerState\n+from research_desk.replay import ReplayEngine\n+\n+_NETWORK_BLOCKED_REPLAY = \"\"\"\n+import json, socket, sys\n+# Block real network I/O without breaking ssl subclassing (keep the class;\n+# patch the connection methods). Any socket that actually tries to connect\n+# raises, proving replay performs zero external calls.\n+def _block(*a, **k):\n+    raise OSError(\"network blocked during offline replay\")\n+socket.socket.connect = _block\n+socket.socket.sendall = _block\n+socket.socket.recv = _block\n+socket.getaddrinfo = _block\n+from research_desk.models import LedgerState\n+from research_desk.replay import ReplayEngine\n+from research_desk.policy import policy_bounds\n+engine = ReplayEngine()\n+pack = engine.load(sys.argv[1])\n+res = engine.replay(pack, sys.argv[2], ledger=None)\n+bounds = None\n+if res.pack.proposal is not None and res.pack.proposal.price is not None:\n+    bounds = policy_bounds(LedgerState(cash=100000.0), res.pack.proposal.price)\n+print(json.dumps({\n+    \"signal\": res.signal,\n+    \"manifest_signal\": res.pack.manifest.signal,\n+    \"reports\": len(res.report_files),\n+    \"external_calls\": res.external_calls,\n+    \"max_by_cap\": None if bounds is None else bounds[\"max_by_cap\"],\n+    \"max_by_cash\": None if bounds is None else bounds[\"max_by_cash\"],\n+}))\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+\n+def test_replay_in_new_process_zero_external_calls(aapl_pack, tmp_path, settings):\n+    \"\"\"AT-01: export to ZIP, replay in a fresh process with networking blocked.\"\"\"\n+    run_dir = settings.runs_dir / aapl_pack.manifest.run_id\n+    shutil.copytree(\"test/fixtures/packs/aapl_buy_complete\", run_dir)\n+    out_dir = tmp_path / \"rebuilt\"\n+    out_dir.mkdir()\n+\n+    start = time.time()\n+    proc = subprocess.run(\n+        [sys.executable, \"-c\", _NETWORK_BLOCKED_REPLAY, str(run_dir), str(out_dir)],\n+        capture_output=True,\n+        text=True,\n+        timeout=60,\n+        env={\"PYTHONPATH\": \".\", \"PATH\": \"/usr/bin:/bin\"},\n+    )\n+    elapsed = time.time() - start\n+    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr\n+    result = json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])\n+    assert result[\"external_calls\"] == 0\n+    assert result[\"signal\"] == \"Buy\"\n+    assert result[\"signal\"] == result[\"manifest_signal\"]\n+    assert result[\"max_by_cap\"] == 100  # 10% of 100000 / 100 == 100 shares\n+    assert result[\"max_by_cash\"] == 1000\n+    assert result[\"reports\"] >= 1\n+    assert elapsed < 2.0, f\"replay took {elapsed:.2f}s, expected < 2s (NFR-001)\"\n+\n+\n+def test_incomplete_pack_fails_clearly(aapl_pack, tmp_path):\n+    \"\"\"AT-01: a deleted required record is reported, not silently replayed.\"\"\"\n+    missing_dir = tmp_path / \"missing-final-state\"\n+    shutil.copytree(\"test/fixtures/packs/aapl_buy_complete\", missing_dir)\n+    (missing_dir / \"final_state.json\").unlink()\n+    engine = ReplayEngine()\n+    with pytest.raises(EvidencePackError, match=\"missing required files\"):\n+        engine.load(missing_dir)\n+\n+\n+def test_empty_final_state_for_completed_run_rejected(tmp_path):\n+    \"\"\"A pack claiming completion with an empty final state cannot replay.\"\"\"\n+    import shutil\n+\n+    d = tmp_path / \"empty-state\"\n+    shutil.copytree(\"test/fixtures/packs/aapl_buy_complete\", d)\n+    (d / \"final_state.json\").write_text(\"{}\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n+    engine = ReplayEngine()\n+    with                "patch": "Index: Report.md\n===================================================================\n--- Report.md\t\n+++ Report.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,214 @@\n+# TradingAgents Research Desk\n+\n+## Project and participant record\n+\n+CS5351 Agentic Software Engineering Project. Participant and evaluation identifier: **leo**. Relative contribution: **1.0**. The implementation extends official TradingAgents **v0.4.0**. Repository: [Fighterforever/cs5351-tradingagents-research-desk](https://github.com/Fighterforever/cs5351-tradingagents-research-desk), private.\n+\n+This project uses a genuine language-model research graph to investigate a practical software engineering question: how can a user inspect the evidence behind an AI recommendation, reproduce its presentation, and control the consequences of accepting it? The delivered workflow connects research to a portable evidence package, then to an explicitly approved paper transaction. A second workflow compares the cost and quality of two context strategies using the same underlying research system.\n+\n+The project was conducted as a teaching evaluation under the identifier leo. The user authorized autonomous decisions and DeepSeek API execution. OpenCode generated application, test and CI code; the coordinating workflow supplied bounded prompts, reviewed declared contracts, executed experiments and prepared documentation. This provenance statement applies to the decision and reflection records throughout the project. No additional students or university student numbers are invented. The repository preserves the real OpenCode sessions and intervention records.\n+\n+The report distinguishes the system's research capability from the authority to change paper state. Research can produce useful reasoning while still being uncertain or incomplete. Execution requires an exact approval and a deterministic policy result. The experiment likewise separates measured token reduction from factual quality. A shorter report earns no quality credit simply because it costs less to generate.\n+\n+## 1. Problem, scope and contribution\n+\n+TradingAgents is a substantial existing multi-agent application. It already separates research perspectives, produces structured decisions and retains research memory. Its reports are valuable to a reader, but an engineering assessment needs additional evidence about how a particular report was produced and what an application may do with it. A saved report alone does not identify every material input or establish that a later action followed the user's approval.\n+\n+Research Desk adds three cohesive features. The first captures a run as a transferable evidence package and reconstructs the report in a new process without external calls. The second turns a completed recommendation into an operator-reviewed proposal and applies a paper transaction only after deterministic checks. The third adds context and request-budget controls, then measures a baseline/compact comparison over six fixed cases. Each feature participates in an end-to-end user workflow rather than existing as an isolated demonstration.\n+\n+The first feature answers the operator's question, “What did this run actually see?” Its package records instrument identity, analysis cutoff, material tool inputs, model requests, model responses and terminal state. Actual provider usage accompanies the calls. The package can be exported as a ZIP and inspected on another machine. The replay path reconstructs saved results, so it has no reason to instantiate a model client. A controlled rerun has a different purpose: it executes the research graph again against the same frozen data, allowing an experiment on context strategy.\n+\n+The second feature answers, “Which action did I approve?” A proposal includes the research evidence reference, direction, price and operator-selected quantity. Approval refers to exact terms. If those terms change, the old approval cannot authorize the new proposal. The policy checks the current ledger at execution time because the user's earlier review cannot freeze cash or holdings indefinitely. Repeating an already completed execution returns the original transaction instead of applying a second financial side effect.\n+\n+The third feature asks whether repeated prompt material can be reduced without damaging evidence-grounded research. The complete selected upstream graph remains in place for both arms. The same DeepSeek model and inference settings are used. The source corpus is fixed before the comparison. Actual token usage supplies the cost measure, while an independent assessment supplies the quality measure. The request budget also provides a concrete degraded-mode behavior: a stopped research run remains inspectable but does not create an approvable recommendation.\n+\n+The scope deliberately fits a single local operator. The application handles US equities with the market and news analysts, retains the downstream researcher/trader/risk roles, and produces English reports. It offers CLI commands and readable report artifacts. It has no broker integration and places no real orders. This boundary makes the safety requirement testable without presenting a classroom paper ledger as a production trading platform.\n+\n+## 2. Existing-system analysis and baseline selection\n+\n+The baseline is the official v0.4.0 tag from TauricResearch/TradingAgents. The tag was verified in the public repository, and its source was copied into the project before extension work. The release was new on the execution date. The project therefore uses a formal pinned version and establishes a local test baseline instead of describing the release as proven by a long operational history.\n+\n+Source analysis identified the actual extension contracts. TradingAgentsGraph accepts selected analysts, configuration and callbacks. Its propagation path returns a terminal graph state and a signal. The report writer consumes that saved state. Instrument resolution and returns reads include direct data paths that are not ordinary model tool calls. The dependency declarations and provider adapters were also examined before selecting how the extension would access DeepSeek.\n+\n+This inspection prevented several false novelty claims. Structured decisions are inherited. Date-aware memory is inherited. Checkpoint and resume behavior is inherited. The verified market snapshot and token-statistics pattern also belong to the upstream project. Research Desk's contribution is the integrated evidence/review/evaluation workflow around those capabilities. The requirements registry lists inherited requirements with source links so a reviewer can distinguish reuse from new behavior.\n+\n+The unmodified upstream test run completed with **649 passed, 2 skipped and 71 subtests passed**. The saved log records the invocation and result. The skips concerned an optional AWS dependency and a live DeepSeek integration test that was not given a key in that baseline invocation. The extension retains the full original tests directory. Later regression checks run both the upstream suite and the additional application tests.\n+\n+The repository layout preserves upstream source and licensing. New application modules live under src/research_desk. New deterministic tests live under test/offline, and API-dependent experiment assets are separated from them. The Python environment belongs to this project. Installing its dependencies does not change the environment used for the separate course assignments. This isolation matters because dependency changes can otherwise create failures in work that the project did not modify.\n+\n+A real extension also needs to be installable. The first generated slice created its modules but initially omitted the necessary src-layout package-discovery configuration. The CLI then failed to import the package. OpenCode corrected pyproject.toml, after which the installed research-desk command ran successfully. This was an integration defect with a clear reproduction, not a reason to replace the application with a standalone script that bypassed packaging.\n+\n+## 3. Requirements engineering and acceptance strategy\n+\n+The machine-readable product requirements document identifies the user, scope and three features. A consolidated registry contains 23 requirements. Each entry has an identifier, type, statement, priority and a fit criterion expressed as a metric, comparison operator, threshold and verification method. Source links identify inherited behavior. Component and test references make the registry useful to implementation and CI rather than merely readable prose.\n+\n+The priorities follow MoSCoW. Correct evidence handling, deterministic authority and complete measurement are Must requirements. A20% token reduction and a compact wall time within110% of baseline are Should targets. This distinction establishes a decision rule before observing results. A measured optimization can miss its target without justifying a weaker approval boundary. Conversely, a passing safety test cannot be used as evidence that the context strategy saved tokens.\n+\n+The strongest invariants have zero-tolerance fit criteria. Every ledger mutation must refer to exact approved terms and passing current-state policy checks. An unapproved, rejected, nontradeable or policy-violating proposal must leave the ledger unchanged. The graph must not gain execution authority from text in a report. No request may begin after the configured call limit. These are operational rules with observable failure behavior, not broad aspirations such as “the system should be safe.”\n+\n+The fixed teaching policy starts with USD100000 cash. Quantities are positive whole shares. Shorting is forbidden. A purchase may not leave one stock above10% of portfolio equity. The price comes from research evidence; the operator cannot type a favorable execution price. The operator chooses quantity and approves it. A valid sell can reduce an owned position, while a sell beyond the holding is rejected. Hold and REVIEW do not produce a tradeable proposal.\n+\n+Eight acceptance specifications cover the important behavior. AT-01 exports and replays a complete package in a new process, then tests an incomplete package. AT-02 checks source availability, cutoff dates and duplicate handling. AT-03 demonstrates a valid approved transaction and repeat execution. AT-04 covers the forbidden execution cases. AT-05 changes approved terms or current portfolio state before execution. AT-06 exercises the actual request limit and critical context preservation. AT-07 compares six paired research runs. AT-08 exercises the six CI gates and their failure paths.\n+\n+The plan and test specifications were approved at **2026-08-31 12:05:17.791955 UTC**. The first recorded OpenCode implementation event occurred at **12:06:32.695 UTC**. The approval file and raw session provide the chronology. A CI gate must validate the dates and referenced tests rather than treating a freely editable APPROVED string as sufficient evidence. The scope of that decision is the three-feature project, not an indefinite authorization to change any future policy.\n+\n+The most useful negative cases correspond to plausible business failures. For example, approving100 shares at USD100 in an empty USD100000 account reaches the cap exactly. An order for101 shares must fail. However, those two tests alone cannot establish a total-position invariant. The review therefore adds a purchase after an existing position. That example distinguishes a correct holdings cap from an implementation that limits only the latest ticket.\n+\n+Requirement volatility was controlled by keeping the feature scope fixed while clarifying ambiguous semantics. The project did not add a web application, extra analyst families or brokerage integration during implementation. The significant clarifications were that no-shorting permits valid sales, the cap applies to total holdings, approval includes quantity and evidence identity, and compact must affect actual per-agent inputs. Those clarifications are recorded in ADR-002 and the defect diary. They arose from reading the implementation against the approved behavior.\n+\n+## 4. Architecture and authority boundaries\n+\n+The selected architecture adds application-owned seams around the real graph. Three candidates were compared: broad modification of upstream internals, an application extension, and a replacement demonstration graph. The evaluation considered preservation of baseline behavior, deterministic authority, evidence coverage, delivery scope and maintenance. The application extension received the strongest design score because it preserves the real AI system while keeping the new transaction policy outside it.\n+\n+The architecture has a clear flow. The operator invokes the CLI. ResearchRunner assembles a configured graph and a run recorder. The graph consumes market/news evidence and produces research state. EvidencePackIO saves the material needed for inspection and replay. A completed tradeable result can create a pending proposal. The operator reviews exact terms. Policy evaluates the current ledger. Storage applies a permitted transaction atomically and records its provenance.\n+\n+```mermaid\n+flowchart TD\n+    A[Operator request] --> B[ResearchRunner]\n+    C[Frozen identity, prices and news] --> B\n+    B --> D[Real TradingAgents graph]\n+    D --> E[Requests, responses, usage and final state]\n+    E --> F[Portable evidence package]\n+    F --> G[Zero-network report replay]\n+    F --> H[Pending proposal]\n+    I[Operator exact-term approval] --> H\n+    H --> J[Current-ledger policy]\n+    J --> K[Paper transaction]\n+```\n+\n+Module ownership follows these responsibilities. Models declares the persistent records. Config owns settings and teaching constants. Evidence captures calls and packages them. Graph_adapter owns the narrow integration with upstream. Context owns assembly and compaction. Budget owns request accounting. Review owns proposal transitions, while policy owns deterministic business decisions. Storage owns SQLite persistence. Replay reconstructs saved outputs, and the CLI exposes these capabilities to the operator.\n+\n+The distinction between policy and storage is important. Policy decides whether the proposed state change is permitted. Storage records that approved change and its result. Neither module asks a model for permission. The graph's available tools contain research capabilities, and no tool grants approval or mutates the ledger. A sentence inside a model report requesting a policy bypass remains text; it is never interpreted as an operator command.\n+\n+Approval refers to exact content. A fingerprint is appropriate for this purpose because it detects a changed combination of material evidence and trade terms. The fingerprint does not replace ordinary release or schema versions. After approval, changing quantity or price requires another review. A transaction also rechecks current cash and holdings because an earlier approved action may have changed the portfolio. These checks protect different boundaries: exact-content binding protects the user's decision, and current-state evaluation protects the portfolio invariant.\n+\n+The REVIEW_REQUIRED state is recoverable. The first implementation correctly refused an unapproved execution but then prevented approval after entering the recovery state. That would leave the operator with a safe failure and no practical path forward. The corrected state machine allows the operator to inspect and approve the current terms. Completed and rejected proposals retain their explicit business meaning. The state-machine tests cover recovery rather than merely asserting that an error occurs.\n+\n+Research and ledger memory have separate purposes. Upstream memory supports reflection on earlier decisions. The paper ledger represents approved positions and cash. Capturing the memory used in a research run makes that run inspectable, but a memory entry cannot authorize a transaction. Each evaluation process uses its own application home so experimental state cannot leak between cases. The application does not claim multiuser service semantics; its supported workflow is a single operator using a local CLI.\n+\n+## 5. Evidence capture, replay and fixed inputs\n+\n+Evidence capture begins at the real boundaries of the system. Model callbacks can record messages, returned content and reported usage. Tool callbacks can capture arguments and results. They do not automatically observe every data read. Source inspection identified identity resolution and return-history paths that bypass ordinary tool calls. The application subclass explicitly records or freezes these paths, closing a material gap in evidence completeness.\n+\n+A package contains a manifest, material input snapshot, event stream, call records, usage summary and terminal state. It can include the proposal and presentation metadata. Completion is a structural claim about required records being present and parseable. A package missing a required record must fail replay rather than silently inventing it. Failed research still retains diagnostic evidence, but its incomplete status cannot become an approved recommendation.\n+\n+Replay reads saved state and reconstructs the reports and structured decision. It does not ask a language model to recreate previous prose. The same package therefore gives an inspectable report even when the API is unavailable. Display timestamps may differ because they describe the reconstruction, while the decision and policy-relevant fields remain stable. The acceptance test starts replay in a fresh process and blocks external access to establish the intended dependency boundary.\n+\n+A controlled rerun has a different contract. It executes the full research graph again, using fixed non-LLM data. Different context may lead the model to request a different indicator window or select a different valid tool argument. An exact lookup table of old tool calls would answer only the original transcript and return missing data for another valid request. That behavior could confound the comparison. The fixed-data adapter therefore derives valid responses from the same underlying market CSV and source corpus.\n+\n+The experiment uses six real equity cases. Prices were retrieved from Yahoo Finance through the installed yfinance library and saved as CSV. Source manifests record retrieval time, row count and latest eligible trading date. Official issuer releases provide the news facts. Availability is tied to the issuer's publication date, not the later retrieval timestamp. The inputs were frozen before final comparison and are preserved with their source identities.\n+\n+| Case | Analysis date | Frozen close, USD | Role in experiment |\n+|---|---|---:|---|\n+| AAPL |2026-07-31|308.9100036621094|Development|\n+| MSFT |2026-07-30|451.1000061035156|Development|\n+| NVDA |2026-08-27|227.97999572753906|Held out|\n+| AMZN |2026-07-31|271.5799865722656|Held out|\n+| META |2026-07-30|539.030029296875|Held out|\n+| GOOGL |2026-07-23|317.69000244140625|Held out|\n+\n+The cases include facts that require careful interpretation. Amazon's reported net income includes a substantial other-income component associated primarily with Anthropic. Alphabet's net income includes large unrealized equity gains. Apple's reported margin and earnings include a tariff-refund effect. Microsoft's release distinguishes GAAP and non-GAAP earnings. These features make factual support more meaningful than a check that a report merely contains the right ticker.\n+\n+The market files remain actual observations. Optional macroeconomic or prediction-market information absent from the fixed corpus receives an explicit unavailable response. The adapter must not fabricate a convenient value to keep a role busy. An unavailable source can be discussed as missing evidence, and the resulting report should state what can be concluded from the information supplied. The model's reasoning does not change the provenance of its inputs.\n+\n+## 6. Context engineering and request budgets\n+\n+The context design has six layers. Instrument identity establishes the subject. Standing constraints establish the analysis cutoff and advisory boundary. Retrieved knowledge supplies market and news evidence. Conversation history carries earlier arguments. Structured state supports continuation. The current task tells a specific role what it must produce. These layers are explicit because compression should remove redundancy without losing the task's controlling facts.\n+\n+The assembly pipeline first filters evidence for eligibility. It then removes repeated material in compact mode, prioritizes essential content and applies a context budget. After compaction, it re-injects critical constraints. Symbol, analysis date, evidence price, source identity and the current task remain visible. Older discussion may be shortened when it repeats facts already present. The compact strategy also requests concise role responses to reduce repeated prose propagated to later roles.\n+\n+Baseline preserves the original substantive input and follows the same graph. It is not padded with duplicate text to manufacture a favorable comparison. Compact retains all selected roles and uses the same model settings. The comparison therefore measures a context strategy rather than an architectural reduction in work. Both the input and output sides of provider usage are reported because concise output can affect later input size as well as the current response.\n+\n+The first generated context implementation focused on past memory. That was a plausible local interpretation of compaction, and its unit tests could demonstrate deduplication. It would provide little benefit in six fresh cases with little memory. The review identified this mismatch before claiming an improvement and directed OpenCode to transform actual per-agent messages. This intervention illustrates why workload analysis matters: a correct local utility can fail to address the dominant cost of the application.\n+\n+The request budget is an operational constraint. The counter must be checked before a real request starts. Merely recording an exceeded budget after a response would still spend the next call. Callback behavior also matters because some frameworks swallow callback exceptions, and structured-output fallbacks may retry a failed call. The acceptance test therefore exercises the invocation boundary with a fake provider and attempts one call beyond the configured limit.\n+\n+A budget-stopped run keeps the evidence collected so far and records a distinct terminal outcome. It does not claim completion and does not create a tradeable proposal. A legitimate run that completes on its final allowed call should remain completed; reaching the numeric limit alone is not proof that another request was blocked. This distinction makes stop reasons useful for both the user and the evaluation.\n+\n+Per-call output limits use the actual provider contract. The project does not treat a rough character-to-token estimate as measured API usage. Character estimates can help select context, but the report's cost comparison comes from actual usage metadata. Judge calls are separately recorded. A reduction in application tokens is therefore not inflated by omitting the cost of quality evaluation from the evidence record.\n+\n+## 7. Verification results and experimental method\n+\n+Verification has three tiers. Structural checks cover installation, module contracts, permissions, requirement schema and static analysis. Regression checks run all earlier test suites. Behavioral checks exercise the approval boundary, evidence replay and research quality. These tiers are complementary. An importable package can still have an incorrect holdings cap, and a passing deterministic ledger test says nothing about whether a research report faithfully cites earnings evidence.\n+\n+The first extension slice converged to **47 passing offline tests**. The saved OpenCode session contains the real failures and fixes. The tests cover the CLI workflow, incomplete package rejection, point-in-time context, approval, denial and recovery. Review after this checkpoint found omitted business semantics and an incomplete experimental adapter. Those findings triggered a focused second implementation round rather than a claim that47 tests established final acceptance.\n+\n+A demonstration fixture uses a USD100 evidence price and a USD100000 initial account. It is intentionally constructed and identified as a fixture. The recorded CLI workflow first rejects execution without approval. After leo approves100 shares, execution leaves USD90000 cash and100 shares. Repeating the execution returns the same transaction and leaves cash unchanged. A separate101-share example fails the10% cap and preserves the original ledger. These commands establish the user-visible workflow without presenting the fixture price as a live market quote.\n+\n+The fixed research experiment contains12 application runs: six cases under baseline and six under compact. AAPL and MSFT are the development cases. NVDA, AMZN, META and GOOGL were reserved before final tuning. The same frozen inputs, complete selected graph, DeepSeek model and inference configuration apply to both arms. Each case has a saved outcome, call count, input tokens, output tokens and measured elapsed time. Independent OS processes may run concurrently, but cases do not share application state.\n+\n+The quality method has deterministic and semantic parts. Identity, analysis date, captured price and recommendation state are checked against the package. Source references must correspond to available corpus evidence. An independent live judge assesses support and relevance using the predeclared rubric, with the same procedure for both arms. A support score of0.8 requires adequately supported main conclusions without a critical fabrication. A relevance score of0.8 requires the core stock/date task to be covered with limited irrelevant material.\n+\n+Citation validity requires a source to support the associated claim, not merely an existing source identifier. Uncited factual claims are reported so that a model cannot improve the citation percentage by deleting citations. The judge receives the fixed evidence and report content, and its raw response remains available. A malformed judgment is an evaluation failure requiring an explicit recovery record. It is never replaced with an invented perfect score.\n+\n+[[LIVE_RESULTS]]\n+\n+The Should targets are evaluated against the saved runs. Total token reduction is one minus compact application tokens divided by baseline application tokens. Quality retention compares the two arms' mean scores, with a maximum permitted decline of0.05. The wall-time ratio compares measured elapsed time under the disclosed execution conditions. Failures and retries remain in the experiment history. Results from a repaired development run do not justify quietly discarding an unfavorable held-out case.\n+\n+## 8. Coding governance, CI and repository evidence\n+\n+AGENTS.md is the single entry point for coding work. It identifies the baseline, reading order, module ownership and verification requirements. Prompt.md asks the coding agent for a concrete plan before code generation and requires a matching approval. Current approval authorizes the recorded scope. Future safety changes require a new ADR and a specific decision. Rules and approval records are owned by leo rather than by the implementation role.\n+\n+The permission model separates planning, building, verification and release. Planning reads requirements and declared interfaces. Building writes approved application and test paths. Verification reads source and evidence and writes results. Release packages reviewed artifacts and uses the authorized private remote. None of these roles needs to read global credential files. The host injects runtime credentials only into the appropriate child process, and they are excluded from saved evidence and submission artifacts.\n+\n+The first five inherited capabilities remain covered by the original regression suite. New acceptance tests map through the requirement trace matrix to their enforcing component and runtime record. Each safety invariant has a concrete fallback: unchanged ledger, explicit rejection, REVIEW_REQUIRED, or an incomplete research state. The project records such outcomes so a reviewer can diagnose why an action stopped rather than seeing an undifferentiated error.\n+\n+The CI design implements six gates. The first validates test approval and chronology. The second runs lint, type and dependency checks and adds checks for safety-relevant changes. The third validates the requirements registry against its schema. The fourth re-evaluates fixed captured evidence against semantic properties for prompt/model changes. The fifth runs all prior regressions. The sixth requires the AI-use log to change when code or prompts change. Negative examples and repaired outcomes provide evidence that these checks can actually reject a change.\n+\n+An offline semantic replay gate has a precise scope. It can recompute factual and structural properties of committed captured outputs. It cannot establish the quality of a newly generated live answer without calling the model. The release evidence therefore includes the actual paired live evaluation as a separate artifact. The project does not rename a deterministic fixture assertion as a fresh language-model judgment.\n+\n+[[GITHUB_RESULTS]]\n+\n+The repository remains private. The original public repository is retained as upstream, and the private course repository is origin. No changes are pushed to TauricResearch. Source history begins from the real upstream baseline and records the extension with concise meaningful commits. The README explains purpose, architecture, setup and test commands, and links to the real GitHub project. Local check success and server-enforced branch protection are recorded separately.\n+\n+## 9. Supervised process and improvements\n+\n+The process began with course-document analysis and existing-source inspection. Requirements and acceptance examples were written before implementation. The initial approved slice connected evidence, review and a paper ledger so there was an early end-to-end workflow. This reduced integration uncertainty before adding the live experiment. The project then used measured failures and code review to choose the next changes.\n+\n+OpenCode's first session generated the application and tests. Its raw record includes implementation attempts, test failures and corrections. The coordinating review examined business contracts instead of relying entirely on the agent's success statement. The review caught the difference between a ticket cap and total holdings, the omission of shares from approval binding, and the unintended rejection of all sales. It also noticed that an empty-memory compaction example could pass while delivering no useful savings on the planned workload.\n+\n+The first session continued cleanup after its offline milestone. The coordinator ended that session and opened a shorter, focused live-evaluation session. This preserved the useful source changes and reduced the cost of repeatedly carrying a large context. The second prompt named the precise defects, fixed corpus, adapter behavior and required live commands. It did not ask the agent to revisit the entire project or produce another broad plan.\n+\n+Work was divided by ownership to avoid conflicting edits. The core OpenCode session handled application and tests. A separate OpenCode session handled CI scripts and schema. Documentation was maintained alongside the source, and a video workflow captured actual CLI commands in an isolated demo home. The remote repository work waited for a concrete local deliverable. This parallel structure used the API waiting time productively while keeping each code owner bounded.\n+\n+Defect trends are described from actual observations rather than invented issue counts. Early failures concerned packaging, context bookkeeping and a recovery transition. Later review findings concerned business semantics and experimental validity. That progression suggests the implementation became mechanically runnable before it fully represented the approved contracts. The improvement was to move from broad test counts to a smaller number of discriminating examples at each authority boundary.\n+\n+Ambiguity resolution is explicit. “No shorting” was interpreted as allowing a sell up to owned shares. “Ten percent position” refers to resulting holdings. “Approval” covers quantity and material evidence. “Replay” reconstructs a saved result, while “rerun” regenerates one from fixed input. “Token reduction” refers to actual provider usage. These definitions are reflected in the requirements, ADRs and tests so later maintenance does not have to reconstruct the reasoning from a conversation.\n+\n+Artifacts co-evolved through the trace matrix. A change to the holdings interpretation affected the policy owner, approval decision, test examples and defect diary. A change to the context strategy affected ADR-001, the runtime adapter and evaluation method. The schema correction made the machine-readable registry validate the document actually committed, rather than an unrelated example record. The AI-use log points to real sessions and their scopes. No artifact is considered complete merely because its filename matches the course checklist.\n+\n+The project also separates review authority from outcome evidence. A decision can authorize a plan, but it cannot declare an unrun test successful. An ADR can select an architecture, but it cannot establish measured token savings. A workflow file can define checks, but it cannot prove a server rejected a merge. This separation made the final deliverable more reviewable and prevented documentation from outrunning implementation.\n+\n+## 10. Limitations and remaining risks\n+\n+The application is a local teaching research desk. Its approval identity is the local operator identifier and does not provide enterprise authentication. It does not connect to a broker or model real execution costs. Portfolio valuation uses the documented evidence/mark convention, and the workload does not establish multiuser concurrency guarantees. A network service would require a separate architecture decision for identity and transaction isolation.\n+\n+The six-case experiment evaluates context engineering on a defined frozen corpus. It does not establish investment profitability, general financial forecasting performance or robustness to every future market regime. Cases include actual prices and official releases, but the selected corpus is smaller than an unrestricted research environment. Independent live judgments remain model assessments and are preserved for inspection. Deterministic facts and policy results do not rely on those judgments.\n+\n+The baseline tag was newly released and is supported here by the recorded regression run. Future upstream or provider changes can invalidate adapter assumptions and require another full test cycle. Offline replay establishes reconstruction of captured state, while a controlled live rerun can produce a different recommendation. Any unavailable external branch-protection capability is described in the GitHub results rather than hidden behind local checks.\n+\n+The project evidence reflects the authorized evaluation workflow under leo. It does not claim the participation of a real three-person student team or human approvals that did not occur. The course's transcript wording varies between one full raw session and five annotated sessions; the submission retains the actual complete sessions and maps their stages without fabricating extra conversations. The exact deployment and experimental outcomes are reported with their saved evidence.\n+\n+## 11. Reflection: leo, evaluation identifier leo\n+\n+The most important lesson from this project was that useful supervision concentrates on the meaning of a contract. The coding agent quickly produced a large runnable slice, and the first successful test run created a natural temptation to treat the implementation as finished. Reading the actual policy showed why that would have been premature. A limit on one purchase looked similar to a limit on the resulting holding, yet the two rules permit different portfolio states. The same issue appeared in approval binding: identifying the symbol and price did not identify the quantity the operator had accepted. Those findings changed my review practice. I looked for a short example that separates the intended behavior from the plausible wrong implementation, then supplied that example to OpenCode. I also learned to distinguish an optimization mechanism from an optimization result. Deduplicating a memory string was valid code, but fresh research cases had little memory to compress. The experiment needed changes at the actual per-agent input boundary and actual provider usage before it could support a cost claim. Keeping the real upstream graph made that reasoning more demanding and more useful because it prevented the project from winning by silently removing work. The evidence package improved my ability to review both kinds of result. It connected a report to its inputs and calls, while the ledger record connected a state change to a concrete approval and policy decision. Parallel work helped when each owner had a bounded responsibility: application code, CI, documentation and the recorded demonstration could progress without rewriting one another's files. Ending an overgrown code session after a useful milestone was another practical improvement. A fresh focused prompt preserved momentum better than asking the same session to keep polishing indefinitely. I would carry these habits into future projects: define observable acceptance examples first, inspect the real interface before instructing an agent, preserve failed evidence, and keep claims proportional to the operation that was actually performed. The project strengthened my understanding that engineering leadership with a coding agent is an active design and review task. It requires choosing the next concrete uncertainty to resolve and maintaining the correspondence between requirements, executable behavior and evidence.\n+\n+## 12. Reproducibility and deliverable map\n+\n+The repository contains the requirements registry and JSON schema under docs/req. Architecture artifacts include the root blueprint, ADRs, invariant register, trace matrix, memory design, permission model, runtime policy catalog and candidate evaluation. Governance files include AGENTS.md, Prompt.md, project rules, structural constraints and verification constraints. The review memo, debt register and defect diary preserve significant decisions and findings.\n+\n+Source is under src/research_desk and the original upstream directories remain intact. Deterministic tests are under test/offline. Frozen public inputs and recorded fixture packages are identified separately. Live evaluation artifacts contain per-case evidence and aggregated results. The transcripts directory preserves sanitized full OpenCode sessions and annotations. The final report is this single Markdown document, with a12-point single-spaced PDF rendering supplied for page-count inspection. The600-second MP4 demonstration is a separate deliverable and is not embedded in the source ZIP.\n+\n+A reviewer should first read the README and run the deterministic suite. The isolated demonstration then shows export, replay, approval, execution and rejection. The live experiment can be repeated with an explicitly provided DeepSeek key and the saved fixed inputs. Repetition may incur API charges and produce different reasoning; the archived original results remain the evidence for this report's numerical claims. The environment lock records the actual installed dependency versions without including local credentials or editable absolute paths.\n+\n+## References\n+\n+1. TauricResearch.                "patch": "Index: architecture-blueprint.md\n===================================================================\n--- architecture-blueprint.md\t\n+++ architecture-blueprint.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@\n+# Architecture blueprint\n+\n+Decision: leo accepted application composition over TradingAgents v0.4.0. Authoritative design: ADR-001. Scope: one local operator, US equities, English reports, market/news analysts and the complete downstream upstream graph. The application supports research, evidence replay, paper execution and controlled context experiments.\n+\n+## Drivers and boundaries\n+\n+The strongest driver is a visible authority boundary between probabilistic research and deterministic portfolio state. Reproducibility requires freezing material data without claiming to recreate stochastic generation. Maintainability requires keeping the upstream graph and tests intact. Cost evaluation requires the same model and graph for both arms, so replacing expensive agents would invalidate this experiment.\n+\n+The operator invokes a CLI. A ResearchRunner constructs the real graph, supplies context and records callbacks. The EvidenceTradingGraph subclass owns data seams that callbacks alone cannot see, including instrument identity and returns reads. Tool adapters supply fixed corpus data during controlled reruns. Research produces a terminal state and evidence package. It never executes a trade.\n+\n+```mermaid\n+flowchart LR\n+  Operator --> CLI\n+  CLI --> Runner[ResearchRunner]\n+  Runner --> Context[Context and request budget]\n+  Context --> Graph[TradingAgentsGraph]\n+  Corpus[Frozen evidence] --> Graph\n+  Graph --> Pack[Evidence package]\n+  Pack --> Replay[Offline replay]\n+  Pack --> Pending[Pending proposal]\n+  Operator --> Review[Exact-term approval]\n+  Review --> Pending\n+  Pending --> Policy[Deterministic current-ledger checks]\n+  Policy --> Ledger[Atomic paper ledger]\n+```\n+\n+## Component ownership\n+\n+| Element | Owning module | Contract |\n+|---|---|---|\n+| Structured records | `models.py` | Explicit persisted fields, normalized statuses and proposal version |\n+| Settings | `config.py` | Home paths and authoritative teaching policy constants |\n+| Evidence recording and package IO | `evidence.py` | Capture actual calls, tool data and direct reads; reject incomplete packages |\n+| Real graph integration | `graph_adapter.py` | Preserve graph roles, freeze non-LLM inputs, derive evidence price |\n+| Context assembly | `context.py` | Preserve critical facts, remove redundant text only in compact mode |\n+| Request budget | `budget.py` | Prevent the next model request at the configured limit |\n+| Approval lifecycle | `review.py` | Exact-term approval, re-review on changed terms, idempotent execution |\n+| Portfolio policy | `policy.py` | Cash, total-position cap and no-short checks without an LLM |\n+| Persistent ledger | `storage.py` | SQLite proposal/position/transaction persistence |\n+| Replay | `replay.py` | Rebuild reports from captured state without creating a model client |\n+| Presentation | `cli.py`, `report.py` | Commands and inspectable Markdown/HTML outputs |\n+\n+The new modules reuse upstream public declarations rather than reimplement agent reasoning. Any additional frozen-corpus or evaluation modules remain application owned and do not change vendor routing.\n+\n+## Authority and execution\n+\n+Only the local operator can approve exact proposal terms. The model supplies a signal and reasoning. The quantity comes from the operator; the price comes from captured evidence. The deterministic policy uses current ledger state immediately before execution. A content fingerprint is appropriate here because approval must refer to exact terms; it is not a release version. SQLite records a single atomic transaction, and repeated execution returns the original result.\n+\n+One research run executes sequentially within a process because upstream configuration has process-level state. Independent evaluation processes may run concurrently with separate homes. The ledger supports the single-operator CLI workflow; this release does not expose a concurrent network trading service.\n+\n+## Verification and observation\n+\n+Structural checks preserve import/module boundaries and governance records. Regression runs include the complete original upstream suite plus the extension tests. Behavioral verification evaluates exact safety examples and six frozen research cases. Events record context decisions, request counts, provider tokens, tool reads, terminal outcome and stop reason. A successful provider response is evidence of execution, not evidence of factual quality.\n+\n+Change policy: new requirements update the registry, trace matrix, tests and affected ADR in the same change. Runtime context changes require fixed-set semantic replay and saved live comparison evidence. Failed or budget-stopped runs remain available and cannot become approved research. See the runtime policy catalog for operational actions.\n",

Requirements: FR-001 through FR-003, INV-001, INV-002. The concrete plan and tests were approved at 12:05:17.791955 UTC before OpenCode's first implementation event at 12:06:32.695 UTC.\n+\n+## Context and alternatives\n+\n+TradingAgents v0.4.0 already provides multi-agent research, structured decisions, date-aware memory, checkpointing and price validation. The missing product workflow is portable evidence followed by explicit approval and paper execution. A complete graph rewrite would discard tested domain behavior and make the optimization baseline incomparable. Editing every upstream prompt and tool would distribute application-specific policy across many owners. A narrow application extension keeps the experimental boundary visible.\n+\n+Candidate A modifies the entire graph and shared vendors. Candidate B subclasses/composes the existing graph and implements policy outside it. Candidate C builds a small new agent demo. The evaluation table selects B because it preserves genuine AI integration while keeping deterministic authority isolated. The original graph's full selected role sequence is retained in both experimental arms.\n+\n+## Context layers and assembly\n+\n+Layer1 identifies the instrument and analysis cutoff. Layer2 states standing constraints: use available evidence, retain source identity, distinguish unknown facts and keep execution advisory. Layer3 supplies frozen market/history/news knowledge. Layer4 holds current discussion and retrieved past context. Layer5 preserves resumable structured state. Layer6 gives the current agent task and expected output.\n+\n+The assembly order is eligibility filtering, duplicate removal in compact mode, prioritization, budget accounting, compaction and final constraint reinjection. Baseline preserves original substantive prompt input. Compact can remove repeated paragraphs or shorten older discussion, while retaining symbol, date, price evidence, source IDs and current task. It also requests concise role output to reduce repeated prose passed to later agents. Fresh six-case runs have little past memory, so compact must apply to actual per-agent messages; changing only a memory string would leave the dominant token cost unchanged.\n+\n+The call budget is configured for the experiment. Per-call maximum output bounds use the provider's existing max_tokens contract. Character estimates may guide context assembly but never replace provider-reported token usage. The model adapter checks before starting a request; a structured-output retry cannot create an extra request after the budget is exhausted. Critical constraints are re-injected after compaction. Factual quality is evaluated independently of brevity.\n+\n+## Consequences and reopening conditions\n+\n+Evidence packs contain prompts and responses and are larger than ordinary reports. Replay is fast because it reconstructs captured state; controlled reruns call the model and remain stochastic. The frozen provider must answer valid parameter variations from data, because an exact tool-transcript lookup would bias the comparison when compact changes tool arguments.\n+\n+The approval boundary stays outside all model tools. The extension retains responsibility for current-ledger checks even if upstream research changes. Reopen this ADR if an upstream public interface cannot expose a material external read, if multiuser concurrency is added, or if compact cannot satisfy factual constraints without discarding agent roles. No such need justifies silently replacing the baseline.\n",

Requirements: FR-002, INV-001, INV-002. This clarifies the approved policy rather than adding a new feature.\n+\n+The first generated implementation treated the10% cap as a limit on one new ticket. It also excluded Sell/Underweight even though the plan prohibited shorting rather than all sales. Its approval fingerprint omitted quantity and evidence identity. These behaviors would allow repeated individually small buys to exceed the policy or allow changed terms to reuse an earlier approval.\n+\n+The correct unit is the total position after a purchase, valued at the current ticker's frozen evidence mark. Other position marks must be explicit under the supported ledger convention. A sell reduces owned shares and is permitted only within that holding. Hold and REVIEW remain nontradeable. Approval binds symbol, date, normalized side, price, shares and material evidence identity. Changed terms cause REVIEW_REQUIRED. The operator can review and approve corrected terms; this state must not become a dead end.\n+\n+The smallest owners are policy.py for business decisions, review.py for binding and transitions, storage.py for signed position updates, and models.py for explicit fields. Upstream agent code has no reason to change. Tests cover a second buy in an existing position, a valid sell, overselling and quantity changes after approval. The source of truth for completion is the final offline test log, not this acceptance decision.\n",

Upstream memory retains structured research decisions for reflection; the application captures exactly the memory used by a run. The paper ledger records approved transactions. A model-generated reflection cannot write the paper ledger.\n+\n+The application home, selected by RESEARCH_DESK_HOME, contains the SQLite database and run directories. Every demonstration and evaluation uses a separate project-local home. SQLite stores proposals, cash, positions and transactions. Evidence files store manifest, material input, events, calls, provider usage and terminal state. A package can be transferred independently of the database for replay. Proposal approval refers to exact evidence and trade terms.\n+\n+A completed run survives process exit through its evidence package. Interrupted or budget-stopped runs retain the terminal reason and collected calls. Replay reconstructs saved state. A controlled rerun creates a new run and refers to its source evidence; it never overwrites the earlier result. Evaluation resumes completed cases to avoid accidental rebilling.\n+\n+Memory retrieval applies the analysis cutoff to resolution/availability dates. Retrieval date is recorded separately because downloading a July release in August does not make its content available before July. Future-resolved lessons are excluded. Unknown availability is visible and unsuitable for strict historical claims. This rule concerns input provenance and does not certify investment validity.\n+\n+The package schema starts at version1. Release names follow ordinary semantic versioning. Content fingerprints serve integrity and exact approval binding only. Changes to persisted contracts need an explicit migration or documented import path before claiming compatibility. No unsupported cross-version restoration is promised.\n+\n+Retention: keep source fixtures, experiment evidence, decisions and sanitized sessions through assessment; retain ledger demonstrations as reproducible fixtures. Credentials are never durable state. User-specific caches, environment files and Yahoo cookies are excluded from the submission and repository. Deleting a project home resets local paper state and must not delete the immutable submitted experiment evidence.\n",

docs/process/PROJECT_PLAN.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@\n+# TradingAgents Research Desk 项目方案\n+\n+状态：leo已采纳，OpenCode正在实现。执行来源统一见 `../orchestration/README.md`。本文指标为验收目标，实测结果在后续报告中单列。\n+\n+## 一、交付范围\n+\n+在现有 Manager，随后保存状态和决策。对源码的查询未找到独立人工批准状态机或模拟账本；README的模拟执行概述不能代替实现证据。\n+\n+保留上游 `tradingagents/`、`cli/` 和 `tests/`。新增模块放 `src/research_desk/`，新增课程测试放 `test/offline/`、`test/live/`，CI同时跑原测试。不要为符合目录树而重写上游代码。\n+\n+## 三、新增需求\n+\n+### F1：研究证据包与离线复现\n+\n+保存分析日期、股票、模型/配置、prompt版本、实际输入资料、LLM请求/结果/usage、报告、决策及本次用到的记忆。导出资料包并生成来源索引。\n+\n+离线复现读取已捕获状态与事件，重建报告和模拟策略结果，完全不调用网络。受控重跑则用冻结资料再次调用LLM，供比较配置；LLM的输出仍可能变化，两种功能需要明确区分。\n+\n+| ID | 优先级 | F3：紧凑上下文与成本对照\n+\n+增加研究调用预算、上下文装配和baseline/compact成对比较。保留股票身份、研究日期、关键价格、站立约束和当前任务；去重重复报告，压缩较旧讨论；压缩后重新加入关键约束。\n+\n+| ID | 优先级 | 需求与fit criterion |\n+|---|---|---|\n+| FR-003 | Must | |\n+\n+新字段显式用已有Pydantic声明；新状态用项目SQLite数据库和运行目录。模拟账本与上游研究记忆分开。第一版顺序执行分析，避免上游进程级配置在并发任务中混用。\n+\n+callbacks不能自动覆盖全部外部数据：identity、回报读取等存在直接数据路径。OpenCode必须先定位这些真实边界，再提出最小接口扩展。禁止全局monkeypatch，禁止在共享vendor路由里按项目名加分支。\n+\n+候选A：全面改图；候选B：应用层加必要的窄接口；候选C：重写多agent。选择B以控制变更范围，保留上游成熟能力和可比较基线。若真实接入限制阻碍证据完整性，则针对具体接口重开ADR。\n+\n+```mermaid\n+flowchart if not line:\n+        return None\n+    # porcelain v1: \"XY path\" (renames/copies include a second path segment).\n+    if len(line) > 3:\n+        return line[3:].split(\" -> \")[0].strip()\n+    return None\n+\n+\n+def changed_files(\n+    root: Path,\n+    base_ref: str | None = None,\n+    head_ref: str | None = None,\n+    explicit: str | None = None,\n+) -> list[str]:\n+    \"\"\"Resolve return []\n+    files = []\n+    for line in proc.stdout.splitlines():\n+        path = _parse_status_line(line)\n+        if path:\n+            files.append(path)\n+    return files\n+\n+\n+def parser.add_argument(\n+        \"--changed-files\",\n+        default=None,\n+        help=\"Comma-separated explicit changed file list (negative-test override).\",\n+    )\n+\n+\n+def fail(checks: This module applies compaction to the\n+actual message inputs each agent sends and to the output-length instruction,\n+by wrapping the real LangChain chat model with a small application-owned\n+delegate that exposes the methods the graph actually uses — ``invoke``,\n+``bind_tools`` and ``with_structured_output`` — while retaining the real\n+LangChain client and upstream ``GraphSetup``.\n+\n+For ``context_mode == \"baseline\"`` the delegate is a no-op: the exact, real\n+uncompressed client is returned unchanged (no artificial padding, no rewrite).\n+For ``compact`` the delegate trims redundant message text, de-duplicates, and\n+appends a concise-output instruction, while preserving key quoted facts (the\n+standing-constraints markers) in every affected prompt.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+from typing import Any\n+\n+from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, BaseMessage, HumanMessage, SystemMessage\n+\n+# Content markers that carry the facts which must survive compaction. pass through unchanged\n+\n+    seen: set[str] = set()\n+    kept: list[BaseMessage] = []\n+    for msg in messages:\n+        content = _content_of(msg)\n+        if not content:\n+            continue\n+        if content in seen:\n+            continue  # drop exact duplicate messages\n+        seen.add(content)\n+        if not _has_fact_marker(content) and len(content) > max_msg_chars:\n+            content = content[:max_msg_chars].rstrip() + \"\\n[... compacted ...]\"\n+        kept.append(_rebuild(msg, content))\n+\n+    kept.append(\n+        SystemMessage(content=_OUTPUT_INSTRUCTION.format(max_tokens=max_output_tokens))\n+    )\n+    return kept\n+\n+\n+def _rebuild(msg: BaseMessage, content: str) -> BaseMessage:\n+    \"\"\"Rebuild a message of the same role with trimmed content (preserve id/name).\"\"\"\n+    if isinstance(msg, AIMessage):\n+        return AIMessage(content=content, id=getattr(msg, \"id\", None), name=getattr(msg, \"name\", None))\n+    if isinstance(msg, HumanMessage):\n+        return HumanMessage(content=content, id=getattr(msg, \"id\", None), name=getattr(msg, \"name\", None))\n+    return SystemMessage(content=content, id=getattr(msg, \"id\", None), name=getattr(msg, \"name\", None))\n+\n+\n+def wrap_for_mode(\n+    llm: Any,\n+    context_mode: str,\n+    *,\n+    max_output_tokens: int = 1800,\n+    max_msg_chars: int = 1500,\n+) -> Any:\n+    \"\"\"Return a compact delegate for ``llm``, or the identical client for baseline.\n+\n+    Baseline returns the *same* object (no wrapping, no rewrite). Compact\n+    returns a lightweight subclass of the real model type that overrides\n+    ``invoke`` to transform the per-agent input; ``bind_tools`` and\n+    ``with_structured_output`` are inherited from the real class and route their\n+    calls back through this overridden ``invoke``.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    if context_mode != \"compact\":\n+        return llm\n+    delegate = llm.model_copy(deep=False)\n+    delegate.__class__ = _make_delegate(type(llm), max_output_tokens=max_output_tokens, max_msg_chars=max_msg_chars)\n+    return delegate\n+\n+\n+def wrap_llm_client_factory(\n+    orig_factory,\n+    context_mode: str,\n+    *,\n+    max_output_tokens: int = 1800,\n+    max_msg_chars: int = 1500,\n+):\n+    \"\"\"Wrap the upstream ``create_llm_client`` so ``get_llm()`` returns a delegate.\n+\n+    Used by the runner to scope compaction to the LLMs a single graph builds,\n+    without touching vendor or graph code. Baseline passes the client through\n+    unchanged.\n+    \"\"\"\n+\n+    def factory(provider: str, model: str, base_url: str | None = None, **kwargs):\n+        client = orig_factory(provider, model, base_url, **kwargs)\n+        if context_mode != \"compact\":\n+            return client\n+\n+        class _WrappedClient:\n+            def __init__(self, inner):\n+                self._inner = inner\n+\n+            def get_llm(self):\n+                return wrap_for_mode(\n+                    self._inner.get_llm(),\n+                    context_mode,\n+                    max_output_tokens=max_output_tokens,\n+                    max_msg_chars=max_msg_chars,\n+                )\n+\n+            def get_provider_name(self):\n+                return self._inner.get_provider_name()\n+\n+            def warn_if_unknown_model(self):\n+                return self._inner.warn_if_unknown_model()\n+\n+            def validate_model(self):\n+                return self._inner.validate_model()\n+\n+        return _WrappedClient(client)\n+\n+    return factory\n+\n+\n+def _make_delegate(cls, *, max_output_tokens: int, max_msg_chars: int) -> type:\n+    class _CompactionDelegate(cls):  # type: ignore[valid-type, misc]\n+        def invoke(self, input, config=None, **kwargs):  # noqa: ANN001\n+            transformed = compact_transform(\n+                input, max_output_tokens=max_output_tokens, max_msg_chars=max_msg_chars\n+            )\n+            return super().invoke(transformed, config, **kwargs)\n+\n+    _CompactionDelegate.__name__ = f\"{cls.__name__}CompactionDelegate\"\n+    return _CompactionDelegate\n",

# TradingAgents Research Desk 项目方案\\n2: \\n3: 状态：供主线程自主采纳的实施方案；应用实现尚未开始。用户已授权教学评估实验中的模拟学生决策，所有此类记录标为leo。指标为验收目标，没有已完成实验结果。\\n4: \\n5: ## 一、交付范围\\n6: \\n7: 在现有 TradingAgents 上交付完整流程：**运行研究 → 保存证据包 → 对照研究配置 → 审阅建议 → 确定性策略校验 → 更新模拟账本**。\\n8: \\n9: 第一版使用 CLI 和 HTML/Markdown 报告。只支持 market/news 分析员、US 股票和英语研究报告，仍沿用上游 bull/bear、research manager、trader、risk 与 portfolio manager 流程。完成可演示的纵向切片后再考虑界面美化，不接真实交易。\\n10: \\n11: 这三功能是可实现的起始范围。课程按 N 名组员提出新增需求，当前实际人数未知；后续按真实人数分配有意义的切片，不能把机械拆分当作个人贡献。\\n12: \\n13: ## 二、基线与只读核对结果\\n14: \\n15: 建议固定官方 [TradingAgents v0.4.0](https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents/tree/v0.4.0)，不用滚动 main。已通过 `git ls-remote --tags` 确认标签存在，并下载只读源码到 `/private/tmp/cs5351-tradingagents-v0.4.0`。包版本为0.4.0，要求Python>=3.10。\\n16: \\n17: v0.4.0于2026-08-31发布，包含日期一致性与恢复修复。它是正式标签，但刚发布，不能声称已长期稳定验证；开始实施时跑一次已有离线测试建立本地基线。[官方变更记录](https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents/blob/v0.4.0/CHANGELOG.md)\\n18: \\n19: 已核对的实际接口：\\n20: \\n21: - `TradingAgentsGraph(selected_analysts, debug, config, callbacks)`。\\n22: - `propagate(company_name, trade_date, asset_type=\\\"stock\\\")` 返回 `(final_state, signal)`，signal可能为REVIEW。\\n23: - `save_reports(final_state, ticker, save_path=None)` 输出报告。\\n24: - 上游已有结构化输出、decision memory、checkpoint、日期过滤、价格验证、token统计。上述能力都属于继承功能，不能算作本组创新。\\n25: - 实际图止于Portfolio Manager，随后保存状态和决策。对源码的查询未找到独立人工批准状态机或模拟账本；README的模拟执行概述不能代替实现证据。\\n26: \\n27: 保留上游 `tradingagents/`、`cli/` 和 `tests/`。新增模块放 `src/research_desk/`，新增课程测试放 `test/offline/`、`test/live/`，CI同时跑原测试。不要为符合目录树而重写上游代码。\\n28: \\n29: ## 三、新增需求\\n30: \\n31: ### F1：研究证据包与离线复现\\n32: \\n33: 保存分析日期、股票、模型/配置、prompt版本、实际输入资料、LLM请求/结果/usage、报告、决策及本次用到的记忆。导出资料包并生成来源索引。\\n34: \\n35: 离线复现读取已捕获状态与事件，重建报告和模拟策略结果，完全不调用网络。受控重跑则用冻结资料再次调用LLM，供比较配置；LLM的输出仍可能变化，两种功能需要明确区分。\\n36: \\n37: | ID | 优先级 | 需求与fit criterion |\\n38: |---|---|---|\\n39: | FR-001 | Must | 一条命令导出完整证据包，新进程可导入并重建报告；列出所有实际调用和运行配置 |\\n40: | NFR-001 | Must | 固定6包离线复现成功率100%，外部调用数0，结构化决策/策略结果相同；本机单包重建<2秒 |\\n41: | SEC-001 | Must | 输出不包含API凭证；所有未来才可用的资料不得用于声明为历史评估的研究 |\\n42: \\n43: 报告生成时间等展示元数据不参与一致性判断。文件摘要仅用于完整性，不充当用户版本号。上游已有价格snapshot；增量是跨输入、运行和结果的可移交证据包。\\n44: \\n45: ### F2：人工批准的模拟账本\\n46: \\n47: 研究结束产生待审阅建议。操作员选择股数并批准，系统根据当前账本、冻结价格与策略判断是否允许模拟执行。状态为 `PENDING_REVIEW → APPROVED/REJECTED → SIMULATED/REVIEW_REQUIRED`。Hold或REVIEW不产生交易。\\n48: \\n49: 初版教学策略：现金USD100000、仅整股、禁止卖空、买入后单股票市值<=组合权益10%。批准绑定具体建议版本，执行前重查当前账本；重复执行同一批准不会重复记账。模型只建议方向和解释，不能设定政策、批准者或余额。\\n50: \\n51: | ID | 优先级 | 需求与fit criterion |\\n52: |---|---|---|\\n53: | FR-002 | Must | 用户可列出建议、看证据、批准/拒绝，观察账本和状态变化 |\\n54: | NFR-002 | Must | 固定允许/拒绝/重复执行案例100%符合策略，策略裁决不调用LLM |\\n55: | INV-001 | Must | 每项账本变化引用已批准建议版本及通过的确定性策略结果；违规次数0 |\\n56: | INV-002 | Must | 未批准、上游REVIEW、资金/持仓不足、超限或价格缺失时不得改变账本；逃逸次数0 |\\n57: \\n58: 操作员直接调用review命令，记录实际本机操作者；研究LLM不能调用review或账本工具。第一版是单机个人工作台，不声称实现企业身份认证。安全失败返回明确的REVIEW_REQUIRED或业务拒绝，并保留账本原状态。\\n59: \\n60: ### F3：紧凑上下文与成本对照\\n61: \\n62: 增加研究调用预算、上下文装配和baseline/compact成对比较。保留股票身份、研究日期、关键价格、站立约束和当前任务；去重重复报告，压缩较旧讨论；压缩后重新加入关键约束。\\n63: \\n64: | ID | 优先级 | 需求与fit criterion |\\n65: |---|---|---|\\n66: | FR-003 | Must | 同一固定资料集输出两种配置的质量、调用数、input/output tokens、wall time和停止原因 |\\n67: | NFR-003 | Must | 达到配置的调用数上限后不开始下一次LLM请求；预算停止结果不可进入可批准建议 |\\n68: | QUALITY-001 | Must | 固定6组资料的强制事实字段正确率100%，引用有效率>=95%，支持度与相关性均>=0.8 |\\n69: | COST-001 | Should | 同模型/资料/范围下compact总tokens降低>=20%，质量平均下降<=0.05 |\\n70: | PERF-001 | Should | compact总wall time不高于baseline的110%，完整报告重试和所有样本 |\\n71: \\n72: 复用上游 `max_tokens` 作为每次输出上限，不另造同名配置。总token必须记录真实usage；不声称不同网关下有精确美元硬上限。2组资料用于开发，另4组在开发前冻结；最终完整跑两种配置各6组。引用、评分和应用token分开记录，避免评估费用被隐藏。\\n73: \\n74: MoSCoW取舍：先保证完整工作流和Must项，成本/性能提升有真实比较后才认定达成；图形界面、更多分析员、并行批处理和券商接入不进入第一版。\\n75: \\n76: ## 四、最小架构\\n77: \\n78: | 新模块 | 责任 | 复用点 |\\n79: |---|---|---|\\n80: | `research.py` | 研究生命周期和RunRecord | TradingAgentsGraph、配置、报告 |\\n81: | `evidence.py` | 调用/输入记录、资料包、离线复现 | callbacks、现有报告写入器 |\\n82: | `context.py` | 选择、去重、压缩、重注入关键约束 | 实际prompt所有者的局部接入 |\\n83: | `budget.py` | 调用预算与实际usage | StatsCallbackHandler的计量方式、上游max_tokens |\\n84: | `review.py` | 批准状态、策略、账本事务 | 最终signal仅作建议输入 |\\n85: | `cli.py` | analyze/export/replay/compare/review命令 | 既有typer/rich |\\n86: \\n87: 新字段显式用已有Pydantic声明；新状态用项目SQLite数据库和运行目录。模拟账本与上游研究记忆分开。第一版顺序执行分析，避免上游进程级配置在并发任务中混用。\\n88: \\n89: callbacks不能自动覆盖全部外部数据：identity、回报读取等存在直接数据路径。OpenCode必须先定位这些真实边界，再提出最小接口扩展。禁止全局monkeypatch，禁止在共享vendor路由里按项目名加分支。\\n90: \\n91: 候选A：全面改图；候选B：应用层加必要的窄接口；候选C：重写多agent。选择B以控制变更范围，保留上游成熟能力和可比较基线。若真实接入限制阻碍证据完整性，则针对具体接口重开ADR。\\n92: \\n93: ```mermaid\\n94: flowchart LR\\n95:     U[操作员] --> C[CLI]\\n96:     C --> R[研究编排]\\n97:     R --> X[上下文与预算]\\n98:     X --> T[TradingAgents / DeepSeek]\\n99:     T --> E[证据包]\\n100:     E --> F[复现与对照报告]\\n101:     E --> P[待审阅建议]\\n102:     U --> A[人工批准]\\n103:     A --> P\\n104:     P --> G[确定性策略]\\n105:     G --> L[模拟账本]\\n106: ```\\n107: \\n108: 记忆设计：记录原始资料、结构化研究结果和模拟账本；每次运行冻结实际使用的上游记忆。先支持同一应用版本恢复，数据schema使用单一语义版本字段；真实格式变化才添加迁移。运行证据保留到课程验收后，删除策略由学生决定；凭证不入库。\\n109: \\n110: ## Entries for\\n334:         other tickers accumulate until that ticker is run again.\\n335:         \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n336:         pending = [e for e in self.memory_log.get_pending_entries() if e[\\\"ticker\\\"] == ticker]\\n337:         if not pending:\\n338:             return\\n339: \\n340:         benchmark = self._resolve_benchmark(ticker)\\n341:         updates = []\\n342:         for entry in pending:\\n343:             raw, alpha, days, resolution_date = self._fetch_returns(\\n344:                 ticker, entry[\\\"date\\\"], benchmark=benchmark,\\n345:             )\\n346:             if raw is None:\\n347:                 continue  # price not available yet — try again next run\\n348:             reflection = self.reflector.reflect_on_final_decision(\\n349:                 final_decision=entry.get(\\\"decision\\\", \\\"\\\"),\\n350:                 raw_return=raw,\\n351:                 alpha_return=alpha,\\n352:                 benchmark_name=benchmark,\\n353:             )\\n354:             updates.append({\\n355:                 \\\"ticker\\\": ticker,\\n356:                 \\\"trade_date\\\": entry[\\\"date\\\"],\\n357:                 \\\"raw_return\\\": raw,\\n358:                 \\\"alpha_return\\\": alpha,\\n359:                 \\\"holding_days\\\": days,\\n360:                 \\\"reflection\\\": reflection,\\n361:                 \\\"resolution_date\\\": resolution_date,\\n362:             })\\n363: \\n364:         if updates:\\n365:             self.memory_log.batch_update_with_outcomes(updates)\\n366: \\n367:     def resolve_instrument_context(self, ticker: str, asset_type: str = \\\"stock\\\") -> str:\\n368:         \\\"\\\"\\\"Resolve ticker identity once and return the full instrument context.\\n369: \\n370:         Deterministic yfinance lookup (cached, fail-open) injected into a\\n371:         context string so every agent anchors to the real company instead of\\n372:         hallucinating one from the price chart (#814). A current-date run returns\\n384:         None, disabling the filter so live behavior and pre-migration entries\\n385:         (which have no stored resolution date) are unaffected.\\n386:         \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n387:         td = str(trade_date)\\n388:         return td if td < datetime.now().strftime(\\\"%Y-%m-%d\\\") else None\\n389: \\n390:     def _run_signature(self, asset_type: str) -> str:\\n391:         \\\"\\\"\\\"Graph-shape inputs that must invalidate a checkpoint if changed.\\n392: \\n393:         Keyed into the checkpoint thread ID so a resume under a different analyst\\n394:         selection, debate/risk depth, or asset mode starts fresh instead of\\n395:         silently continuing the previous graph (#1089).\\n396:         \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n397:         return \\\"|\\\".join([\\n398:             \\\"analysts=\\\" + \\\",\\\".join(self.selected_analysts),\\n399:             f\\\"debate={self.config['max_debate_rounds']}\\\",\\n400:             f\\\"risk={self.config['max_risk_discuss_rounds']}\\\",\\n401:             f\\\"asset={asset_type}\\\",\\n402:         ])\\n403: \\n404:     def propagate(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \\\"stock\\\"):\\n405:         \\\"\\\"\\\"Run the trading agents graph for a company on a specific date.\\n406: \\n407:         ``asset_type`` selects between the stock pipeline (default) and the\\n408:         crypto pipeline (``\\\"crypto\\\"``) shipped in #567 — the CLI auto-detects\\n409:         from the ticker; programmatic callers pass it explicitly. When\\n410:         ``checkpoint_enabled`` is set in config, the graph is recompiled with\\n411:         a per-ticker SqliteSaver so a crashed run can resume from the last\\n412:         successful node on a subsequent invocation with the same ticker+date.\\n413: \\n414:         Returns ``(final_state, signal)`` where ``signal`` is one of the 5-tier\\n415:         ratings (Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell) or ``\\\"REVIEW\\\"``\\n416:         when the decision had no parseable rating (#1170); guard with\\n417:         ``tradingagents.agents.utils.rating.is_review`` before mapping it to the\\n418:         PortfolioRating enum.\\n419:         \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n420:         self.ticker = company_name\\n421: \\n422:         # Resolve any pending memory-log entries for this ticker before the pipeline runs.\\n423:         self._resolve_pending_entries(company_name)\\n424: \\n425:         with self.checkpoint_scope(company_name, trade_date, asset_type) as thread_id_value:\\n426:             return self._run_graph(\\n427:                 company_name, trade_date, asset_type=asset_type,\\n428:                 checkpoint_thread_id=thread_id_value,\\n429:             )\\n430: \\n431:     def begin_checkpoint(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \\\"stock\\\") -> str | None:\\n432:         \\\"\\\"\\\"Recompile the graph with a per-ticker checkpointer and return the\\n433:         ``thread_id`` to inject into the stream/invoke ``config`` (or ``None``\\n434:         when checkpointing is disabled).\\n435: \\n436:         Pair every call with :meth:`end_checkpoint` in a ``finally``.
