assembly for research runs: baseline vs compact.\\n\\nThe upstream graph already injects a ``past_context`` (memory lessons) and an\\n``instrument_context`` (resolved identity) into the initial state. This module\\nowns the *assembly of that context string* so a compact configuration can\\ngenuinely shrink the prompt while preserving the invariants the task requires:\\n\\n- stock identity, analysis date, key prices,\\n- standing constraints (the simulated policy numbers), current task,\\n- de-duplicated repeated text,\\n- bounded earlier history.\\n\\nCompaction never removes agents or the graph; it only changes the text that is\\nassembled into the initial ``past_context``. The honest size metric recorded\\noffline is the number of characters assembled; actual LLM token usage comes\\nfrom provider ``usage_metadata`` during a run.\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\\nfrom typing import Any\\n\\nfrom .models import ContextMode\\n\\n\\n@dataclass\\nclass StandingConstraints:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Identity/date/price/policy facts that must survive compaction.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n    ticker: str = \\\"\\\"\\n    trade_date: str = \\\"\\\"\\n    identity: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)\\n    prices: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)  # label -> last price\\n    policy: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)  # teaching policy numbers\\n    current_task: str = \\\"\\\"\\n\\n    def header_text(self) -> str:\\n        lines = [\\\"STANDING ANALYSIS CONSTRAINTS (always true for this run):\\\"]\\n        lines.append(f\\\"- Instrument identity: {self.ticker}\\\")\\n        if self.identity.get(\\\"company_name\\\"):\\n            lines.append(f\\\"- Company: {self.identity['company_name']}\\\")\\n        if self.identity.get(\\\"sector\\\"):\\n            lines.append(f\\\"- Sector/industry: {self.identity['sector']} / {self.identity.get('industry', '')}\\\")\\n        lines.append(f\\\"- Analysis date: {self.trade_date}\\\")\\n        for label, price in self.prices.items():\\n            lines.append(f\\\"- Key price ({label}): {price}\\\")\\n        for key, value in self.policy.items():\\n            lines.append(f\\\"- Standing constraint - {key}: {value}\\\")\\n        if self.current_task:\\n            lines.append(f\\\"- Current task: {self.current_task}\\\")\\n        return \\\"\\\\n\\\".join(lines)\\n\\n\\ndef dedup_repeated_blocks(text: str) -> str:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Remove exact duplicate paragraph blocks, keeping first occurrence order.\\n\\n    Operates on blank-line-separated blocks so repeated analyst reports in a\\n    long history collapse to one copy instead of being sent N times.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if not text:\\n        return text\\n    blocks = [b for b in text.split(\\\"\\\\n\\\\n\\\")]\\n    seen: set[str] = set()\\n    kept: list[str] = []\\n    for block in blocks:\\n        key = block.strip()\\n        if not key:\\n            continue\\n        if key in seen:\\n            continue\\n        seen.add(key)\\n        kept.append(block)\\n    return \\\"\\\\n\\\\n\\\".join(kept)\\n\\n\\ndef bound_history(text: str, max_chars: int = 6000) -> str:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Bound total assembled history length by truncating from the tail.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if not text:\\n        return text\\n    if len(text) <= max_chars:\\n        return text\\n    # Cut at a block boundary near the limit so we never split mid-paragraph.\\n    cut = text.rfind(\\\"\\\\n\\\\n\\\", 0, max_chars)\\n    if cut == -1:\\n        cut = max_chars\\n    return text[:cut].rstrip() + \\\"\\\\n\\\\n[... earlier history truncated ...]\\\"\\n\\n\\ndef estimate_token_heuristic(text: str) -> int:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Deterministic English-token heuristic for offline comparisons.\\n\\n    This is a *character-based heuristic*, explicitly NOT claimed as provider\\n    token counts; real token numbers come from LLM usage metadata. It exists so\\n    offline tests can assert that compact genuinely assembles less context.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if not text:\\n        return 0\\n    return max(1, (len(text) + 3) // 4)\\n\\n\\n@dataclass\\nclass AssemblyResult:\\n    text: str\\n    mode: str\\n    chars: int\\n    blocks: int\\n    token_heuristic: int\\n    deduplicated: int = 0\\n    truncated: bool = False\\n\\n\\nclass ContextAssembler:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Assembles the injected ``past_context`` for baseline or compact runs.\\n\\n    Baseline keeps the raw memory text (matching upstream behavior) but still\\n    re-injects the standing constraints so both arms share the same invariants.\\n    Compact additionally de-duplicates repeated blocks and bounds earlier\\n    history, then re-appends the constraints. The same assembler, same source\\n    material, and same graph are used for both arms — only the assembly differs.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n    DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS = 6000\\n    DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES = 5\\n\\n    def __init__(self, constraints: StandingConstraints | None = None, **kwargs):\\n        self.constraints = constraints or StandingConstraints()\\n        self.max_chars = kwargs.get(\\\"max_chars\\\", self.DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS)\\n        self.max_entries = kwargs.get(\\\"max_entries\\\", self.DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES)\\n\\n    def assemble(self, memory_text: str, mode: str | ContextMode) -> AssemblyResult:\\n        mode = ContextMode(mode)\\n        constraints = self.constraints.header_text()\\n        if mode == ContextMode.BASELINE:\\n            body = dedup_repeated_blocks(memory_text)\\n            truncated = len(body) > self.max_chars\\n            body = bound_history(body, self.max_chars)\\n            text = _join_parts(constraints, body)\\n        else:\\n            body = dedup_repeated_blocks(memory_text)\\n            deduped = len(memory_text.split(\\\"\\\\n\\\\n\\\")) - len(body.split(\\\"\\\\n\\\\n\\\")) if memory_text else 0\\n            truncated = len(body) > self.max_chars\\n            body = bound_history(body, self.max_chars)\\n            text = _join_parts(constraints, body)\\n        return AssemblyResult(\\n            text=text,\\n            mode=mode.value,\\n            chars=len(text),\\n            blocks=len([b for b in text.split(\\\"\\\\n\\\\n\\\") if b.strip()]),\\n            token_heuristic=estimate_token_heuristic(text),\\n            deduplicated=deduped,\\n            truncated=truncated,\\n        )\\n\\n    def assemble_from_entries(\\n        self, entries: list[dict[str, Any]], mode: str | ContextMode\\n    ) -> AssemblyResult:\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"Assemble from structured memory entries (TradingMemoryLog shape).\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        if not entries:\\n            return self.assemble(\\\"\\\", mode)\\n        parts = []\\n        for e in entries:\\n            tag = (\\n                f\\\"[{e.get('date', '')} | {e.get('ticker', '')} | \\\"\\n                f\\\"{e.get('rating', '')}]\\\"\\n            )\\n            decision = (e.get(\\\"decision\\\") or \\\"\\\").strip()\\n            reflection = (e.get(\\\"reflection\\\") or \\\"\\\").strip()\\n            block = tag\\n            if decision:\\n                block += f\\\"\\\\nDECISION:\\\\n{decision}\\\"\\n            if reflection:\\n                block += f\\\"\\\\nREFLECTION:\\\\n{reflection}\\\"\\n            parts.append(block)\\n        recent = parts[-self.max_entries :]\\n        return self.assemble(\\\"\\\\n\\\\n\\\".join(recent), mode)\\n\\n\\ndef _join_parts(constraints: str, body: str) -> str:\\n    if not body:\\n        return constraints\\n    return constraints + \\\"\\\\n\\\\n\\\" + body\\n\"},\"output\":\"Wrote file teaching-policy engine for the simulated ledger.\\n\\nThe policy is decided by leo (the simulated student), never by an LLM. Every\\ncheck returns a plain list of human-readable results; the review layer turns a\\nnon-empty list of failures into a business rejection and leaves the ledger\\nuntouched (INV-002). Boundary behaviour is explicit: a position value exactly\\nequal to 10% of equity is allowed (<=), one share more is rejected.\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\\n\\nfrom .config import INITIAL_CASH, MAX_POSITION_PCT, NO_SHORTING\\nfrom .models import LedgerState\\n\\n\\n@dataclass\\nclass PolicyVerdict:\\n    allowed: bool\\n    checks: list[dict]  # each: {\\\"check\\\": str, \\\"passed\\\": bool, \\\"detail\\\": str}\\n    equity: float | None = None\\n    position_value: float | None = None\\n    cash_after: float | None = None\\n\\n\\nclass PolicyViolation(Exception):\\n    def __init__(self, reasons: list[str]):\\n        self.reasons = reasons\\n        super().__init__(\\\"; \\\".join(reasons))\\n\\n\\ndef evaluate_buy(\\n    ledger: LedgerState,\\n    shares: int,\\n    price: float,\\n    *,\\n    initial_cash: float = INITIAL_CASH,\\n    max_position_pct: float = MAX_POSITION_PCT,\\n) -> PolicyVerdict:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Evaluate a buy proposal against the current ledger.\\n\\n    Rules (v1 teaching policy):\\n    1. shares must be a positive integer.\\n    2. price must be positive and present (it always comes from evidence).\\n    3. cost (shares * price) must not exceed available cash.\\n    4. after the buy, the new position market value must be <= 10% of equity.\\n    5. no shorting (v1 is buy-only; sell proposals are rejected here).\\n\\n    ``initial_cash`` is recorded for the ledger seed; the effective cash check\\n    uses the current ledger's cash, which is ``initial_cash`` plus the sum of\\n    prior cash deltas.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    checks: list[dict] = []\\n\\n    def check(name: str, passed: bool, detail: str) -> None:\\n        checks.append({\\\"check\\\": name, \\\"passed\\\": passed, \\\"detail\\\": detail})\\n\\n    if not isinstance(shares, int) or shares <= 0:\\n        check(\\\"integer_positive_shares\\\", False, f\\\"shares must be a positive integer, got {shares!r}\\\")\\n        return PolicyVerdict(False, checks)\\n\\n    if price is None or not isinstance(price, (int, float)) or price <= 0:\\n        check(\\\"price_from_evidence\\\", False, f\\\"price must be a positive number from evidence, got {price!r}\\\")\\n        return PolicyVerdict(False, checks)\\n\\n    equity = ledger.equity\\n    position_value = shares * price\\n    cash_after = ledger.cash - position_value\\n\\n    check(\\\"cash_sufficient\\\", cash_after >= -1e-9, f\\\"cost={position_value:.2f}, cash={ledger.cash:.2f}\\\")\\n\\n    cap_value = max_position_pct * equity\\n    check(\\n        \\\"position_cap_10pct\\\",\\n        position_value <= cap_value + 1e-9,\\n        f\\\"position={position_value:.2f} <= {max_position_pct:.0%} * equity={cap_value:.2f}\\\",\\n    )\\n\\n    check(\\\"no_shorting\\\", NO_SHORTING, \\\"v1 policy is buy-only; sells are not executed\\\")\\n\\n    return PolicyVerdict(\\n        allowed=all(c[\\\"passed\\\"] for c in checks),\\n        checks=checks,\\n        equity=equity,\\n        position_value=position_value,\\n        cash_after=cash_after,\\n    )\\n\\n\\ndef raise_for_violations(verdict: PolicyVerdict) -> None:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Raise a PolicyViolation listing every failed check (no partial writes).\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if not verdict.allowed:\\n        reasons = [f\\\"{c['check']}: {c['detail']}\\\" for c in verdict.checks if not c[\\\"passed\\\"]]\\n        raise PolicyViolation(reasons)\\n\\n\\ndef reject_reasons(verdict: PolicyVerdict) -> list[str]:\\n    return [f\\\"{c['check']}: {c['detail']}\\\" for c in verdict.checks if not review state machine and simulated-ledger execution.\\n\\nFlow: research produces a PENDING_REVIEW proposal. A trusted CLI operator\\napproves or rejects it. Execution re-evaluates the *current* ledger against the\\ndeterministic policy before writing; the approval binds the exact proposal\\nversion, so a changed proposal cannot ride an old approval. Re-executing an\\nalready-simulated proposal is a no-op (idempotence).\\n\\nNo LLM path reaches this module: the research graph only ever writes a proposal\\nin PENDING_REVIEW, and only the CLI review/execute/ledger commands touch it.\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nimport uuid\\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\\n\\nfrom .models import (\\n    ExecutionRecord,\\n    ProposalRecord,\\n    ProposalStatus,\\n    TransactionRecord,\\n    TransactionStatus,\\n    make_proposal_version,\\n    utcnow_iso,\\n)\\nfrom .policy import PolicyViolation, evaluate_buy, raise_for_violations\\n\\n\\nclass ReviewError(Exception):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Business rejection with a stable message; the ledger stays unchanged.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n\\ndef _proposal_content_version(proposal: ProposalRecord) -> str:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Fingerprint of the proposal's tradeable inputs, independent of status.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    return make_proposal_version(\\n        proposal.ticker, proposal.trade_date, proposal.signal, proposal.price\\n    )\\n\\n\\ndef create_proposal(\\n    *,\\n    run_id: str,\\n    ticker: str,\\n    trade_date: str,\\n    signal: str,\\n    rating: str | None,\\n    price: float | None,\\n    proposal_id: str | None = None,\\n) -> ProposalRecord:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Create a PENDING_REVIEW proposal from a completed research run.\\n\\n    Only tradeable signals become proposals. Hold/REVIEW (and any signal the\\n    graph marked REVIEW) never produce a tradeable recommendation, matching the\\n    requirement that REVIEW and Hold do not trade.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if signal in (\\\"Hold\\\", \\\"REVIEW\\\", \\\"Sell\\\", \\\"Underweight\\\"):\\n        raise ReviewError(\\n            f\\\"signal {signal!r} is not tradeable in v1; no proposal is created \\\"\\n            \\\"(REVIEW and Hold do not trade)\\\"\\n        )\\n    pid = proposal_id or f\\\"prop-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}\\\"\\n    return ProposalRecord(\\n        proposal_id=pid,\\n        run_id=run_id,\\n        ticker=ticker,\\n        trade_date=trade_date,\\n        signal=signal,\\n        rating=rating,\\n        price=price,\\n        status=ProposalStatus.PENDING_REVIEW,\\n        proposal_version=_proposal_content_version(\\n            ProposalRecord(\\n                proposal_id=pid,\\n                run_id=run_id,\\n                ticker=ticker,\\n                trade_date=trade_date,\\n                signal=signal,\\n                rating=rating,\\n                price=price,\\n            )\\n        ),\\n        created_at=utcnow_iso(),\\n    )\\n\\n\\ndef approve(\\n    proposal: ProposalRecord,\\n    *,\\n    shares: int,\\n    operator: str,\\n) -> ProposalRecord:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Approve an exact proposal version with an operator-supplied share count.\\n\\n    The approval is bound to the proposal's *content* version, so if the run's\\n    material inputs (ticker/date/signal/price) later change, the old approval\\n    no longer matches and execution requires review.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.SIMULATED:\\n        raise ReviewError(f\\\"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is already simulated\\\")\\n    if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.REJECTED:\\n        raise ReviewError(f\\\"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is rejected and cannot be approved\\\")\\n    if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED:\\n        raise ReviewError(\\n            f\\\"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is REVIEW_REQUIRED; re-approve after review\\\"\\n        )\\n    if not operator:\\n        raise ReviewError(\\\"approval requires an operator identity\\\")\\n    if not isinstance(shares, int) or shares <= 0:\\n        raise ReviewError(f\\\"shares must be a positive integer, got {shares!r}\\\")\\n    if proposal.price is None or proposal.price <= 0:\\n        raise ReviewError(\\n            f\\\"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} has no evidence price; cannot approve without price\\\"\\n        )\\n    proposal.shares = shares\\n    proposal.operator = operator\\n    proposal.status = ProposalStatus.APPROVED\\n    proposal.approved_at = utcnow_iso()\\n    proposal.approved_version = _proposal_content_version(proposal)\\n    return proposal\\n\\n\\ndef reject(proposal: ProposalRecord, *, operator: str, reason: str = \\\"rejected by operator\\\") -> ProposalRecord:\\n    if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.SIMULATED:\\n        raise ReviewError(f\\\"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is already simulated\\\")\\n    proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REJECTED\\n    proposal.operator = operator\\n    proposal.reason = reason\\n    return proposal\\n\\n\\ndef execute(\\n    store, proposal: ProposalRecord, *, operator: str,\\n) -> tuple[ProposalRecord, ExecutionRecord]:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Re-evaluate the current ledger and simulate the approved buy (or reject).\\n\\n    Steps (each observable, none partial):\\n    1. Idempotence: an already-SIMULATED proposal returns its stored execution.\\n    2. Version binding: the current proposal content must match the approved\\n       version; otherwise REVIEW_REQUIRED (AT-05).\\n    3. Re-read the current ledger and run the deterministic policy.\\n    4. On any failure: return REVIEW_REQUIRED / BLOCKED with reasons; ledger\\n       unchanged. On success: apply the transaction atomically.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.SIMULATED:\\n        return proposal, (proposal.execution or ExecutionRecord(executed=True, reason=\\\"already executed\\\"))\\n\\n    current_version = _proposal_content_version(proposal)\\n    if proposal.status != ProposalStatus.APPROVED or proposal.approved_version != current_version:\\n        proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED\\n        proposal.reason = (\\n            \\\"approval no longer matches the proposal content (version changed \\\"\\n Context: F1.\\n\\n## Decision\\n\\nAn evidence pack is a self-contained directory (or a ZIP of one) with a fixed\\nset of JSON/JSONL files: `manifest.json`, `input.json`, `events.jsonl`,\\n`final_state.json`, `usage.json`, `calls.json`, optional `proposal.json`, and\\n`meta.json`. `complete` is only set when every required file is present and\\nparses. Import validates required files and fails loudly on a missing record.\\n\\nReplay rebuilds the report tree from `final_state`, derives the signal with the\\nsame deterministic heuristic the graph uses (`SignalProcessor`), and reports\\nthe deterministic policy bounds for the proposal against a ledger. Replay never\\nconstructs an LLM client.\\n\\n## Why\\n\\n- The final graph state plus the captured tool data are the *material* needed\\n  to rebuild reports and policy outputs with zero external calls; LLM re-output\\n  is not needed and would violate \\\"no network on replay\\\".\\n- Complete/incomplete is a structural property (required files) so a partial\\n  pack cannot silently replay a wrong decision.\\n- JSONL events keep the log append-friendly and streamable.\\n\\n## Consequences\\n\\n- Evidence packs can be large (they keep full prompts/responses for provenance).\\n- Replay is deterministic for the signal and policy; Participant and evaluation identifier: **leo**. Relative contribution: **1.0**. The implementation extends official TradingAgents **v0.4.0**. Repository: [Fighterforever/cs5351-tradingagents-research-desk](https://github.com/Fighterforever/cs5351-tradingagents-research-desk), private.\n+CS5351 Agentic Software Engineering Project. Participant and evaluation identifier: **leo**. Relative contribution: **1.0**. The implementation extends official TradingAgents **v0.4.0**. Repository: [Fighterforever/cs 5351-tradingagents-research-desk](https://github.com/Fighterforever/cs 5351-tradingagents-research-desk), private.\n \n This project uses a genuine language-model research graph to investigate a practical software engineering question: how can a user inspect the evidence behind an AI recommendation, reproduce its presentation, and control the consequences of accepting it? The delivered workflow connects research to a portable evidence package, then to an explicitly approved paper transaction. A second workflow compares the cost and quality of two context strategies using the same underlying research system.\n \n The project was conducted as a teaching evaluation under the identifier leo. The user authorized autonomous decisions and DeepSeek API execution. OpenCode generated application, test and CI code; the coordinating workflow supplied bounded prompts, reviewed declared contracts, executed experiments and prepared documentation. This provenance statement applies to the decision and reflection records throughout the project. No additional students or university student numbers are invented. The repository preserves the real OpenCode sessions and intervention records.\n \n The report distinguishes the system's research capability from the authority to change paper state. Research can produce useful reasoning while still being uncertain or incomplete. Execution requires an exact approval and a deterministic policy result. The experiment likewise separates measured token reduction from factual quality. A shorter report earns no quality credit simply because it costs less to generate.\n \n ## 1. Problem, scope and contribution\n \n TradingAgents is a substantial existing multi-agent application. It already separates research perspectives, produces structured decisions and retains research memory. Its reports are valuable to a reader, but an engineering assessment needs additional evidence about how a particular report was produced and what an application may do with it. A saved report alone does not identify every material input or establish that a later action followed the user's approval.\n \n Research Desk adds three cohesive features. The first captures a run as a transferable evidence package and reconstructs the report in a new process without external calls. The second turns a completed recommendation into an operator-reviewed proposal and applies a paper transaction only after deterministic checks. The third adds context and request-budget controls, then measures a baseline/compact comparison over six fixed cases. Each feature participates in an end-to-end user workflow rather than existing as an isolated demonstration.\n \n The first feature answers the operator's question, “What did this run actually see?” Its package records instrument identity, analysis cutoff, material tool inputs, model requests, model responses and terminal state. Actual provider usage accompanies the calls. The package can be exported as a ZIP and inspected on another machine. The replay path reconstructs saved results, so it has no reason to instantiate a model client. A controlled rerun has a different purpose: it executes the research graph again against the same frozen data, allowing an experiment on context strategy.\n \n The second feature answers, “Which action did I approve?” A proposal includes the research evidence reference, direction, price and operator-selected quantity. Approval refers to exact terms. If those terms change, the old approval cannot authorize the new proposal. The policy checks the current ledger at execution time because the user's earlier review cannot freeze cash or holdings indefinitely. Repeating an already completed execution returns the original transaction instead of applying a second financial side effect.\n \n The third feature asks whether repeated prompt material can be reduced without damaging evidence-grounded research. The complete selected upstream graph remains in place for both arms. The same DeepSeek model and inference settings are used. The source corpus is fixed before the comparison. Actual token usage supplies the cost measure, while an independent assessment supplies the quality measure. The request budget also provides a concrete degraded-mode behavior: a stopped research run remains inspectable but does not create an approvable recommendation.\n \n The scope deliberately fits a single local operator. The application handles US equities with the market and news analysts, retains the downstream researcher/trader/risk roles, and produces English reports. It offers CLI commands and readable report artifacts. It has no broker integration and places no real orders. This boundary makes the safety requirement testable without presenting a classroom paper ledger as a production trading platform.\n \n ## 2. Existing-system analysis and baseline selection\n \n The baseline is the official v0.4.0 tag from TauricResearch/TradingAgents. The tag was verified in the public repository, and its source was copied into the project before extension work. The release was new on the execution date. The project therefore uses a formal pinned version and establishes a local test baseline instead of describing the release as proven by a long operational history.\n \n Source analysis identified the actual extension contracts. TradingAgentsGraph accepts selected analysts, configuration and callbacks. Its propagation path returns a terminal graph state and a signal. The report writer consumes that saved state. Instrument resolution and returns reads include direct data paths that are not ordinary model tool calls. The dependency declarations and provider adapters were also examined before selecting how the extension would access DeepSeek.\n \n This inspection prevented several false novelty claims. Structured decisions are inherited. Date-aware memory is inherited. Checkpoint and resume behavior is inherited. The verified market snapshot and token-statistics pattern also belong to the upstream project. Research Desk's contribution is the integrated evidence/review/evaluation workflow around those capabilities. The requirements registry lists inherited requirements with source links so a reviewer can distinguish reuse from new behavior.\n \n The unmodified upstream test run completed with **649 passed, 2 skipped and 71 subtests passed**. The saved log records the invocation and result. The skips concerned an optional AWS dependency and a live DeepSeek integration test that was not given a key in that baseline invocation. The extension retains the full original tests directory. Later regression checks run both the upstream suite and the additional application tests.\n \n The repository layout preserves upstream source and licensing. New application modules live under src/research_desk. New deterministic tests live under test/offline, and API-dependent experiment assets are separated from them. The Python environment belongs to this project. Installing its dependencies does not change the environment used for the separate course assignments. Reflection: leo, evaluation identifier leo\n \n The most important lesson from this project was that useful supervision concentrates on the meaning of a contract. The coding agent quickly produced a large runnable slice, and the first successful test run created a natural temptation to treat the implementation as finished. Reading the actual policy showed why that would have been premature. A limit on one purchase looked similar to a limit on the resulting holding, yet the two rules permit different portfolio states. The same issue appeared in approval binding: identifying the symbol and price did not identify the quantity the operator had accepted. Those findings changed my review practice. I looked for a short example that separates the intended behavior from the plausible wrong implementation, then supplied that example to OpenCode. I also learned to distinguish an optimization mechanism from an optimization result. Deduplicating a memory string was valid code, but fresh research cases had little memory to compress. The experiment needed changes at the actual per-agent input boundary and actual provider usage before it could support a cost claim. Keeping the real upstream graph made that reasoning more demanding and more useful because it prevented the project from winning by silently removing work. The evidence package improved my ability to review both kinds of result. It connected a report to its inputs and calls, while the ledger record connected a state change to a concrete approval and policy decision. Parallel work helped when each owner had a bounded responsibility: application code, CI, documentation and the recorded demonstration could progress without rewriting one another's files. Ending an overgrown code session after a useful milestone was another practical improvement. A fresh focused prompt preserved momentum better than asking the same session to keep polishing indefinitely. I would carry these habits into future projects: define observable acceptance examples first, inspect the real interface before instructing an agent, preserve failed evidence, and keep claims proportional to the operation that was actually performed. The project strengthened my understanding that engineering leadership with a coding agent is an active design and review task. It requires choosing the next concrete uncertainty to resolve and maintaining the correspondence between requirements, executable behavior and evidence.\n \n ## 12.                "file": "docs/architecture/adr/001-application-extension.md",
               "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/adr/001-application-extension.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/adr/001-application-extension.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/adr/001-application-extension.md\t\n@@ -1,23 +1,27 @@\n # ADR-001: Extend the existing graph through application-owned seams\n \n Status: accepted by leo, 2026-08-31. Requirements: FR-001 through FR-003, INV-001, INV-002. The concrete plan and tests were approved at 12:05:17.791955 UTC before OpenCode's first implementation event at 12:06:32.695 UTC.\n \n ## Context and alternatives\n \n TradingAgents v0.4.0 already provides multi-agent research, structured decisions, date-aware memory, checkpointing and price validation. The missing product workflow is portable evidence followed by explicit approval and paper execution. A complete graph rewrite would discard tested domain behavior and make the optimization baseline incomparable. Editing every upstream prompt and tool would distribute application-specific policy across many owners. A narrow application extension keeps the experimental boundary visible.\n \n Candidate A modifies the entire graph and shared vendors. Candidate B subclasses/composes the existing graph and implements policy outside it. Candidate C builds a small new agent demo. The evaluation table selects B because it preserves genuine AI integration while keeping deterministic authority isolated. The original graph's full selected role sequence is retained in both experimental arms.\n \n ## Context layers and assembly\n \n Layer1 identifies the instrument and analysis cutoff. Layer2 states standing constraints: use available evidence, retain source identity, distinguish unknown facts and keep execution advisory. Layer3 supplies frozen market/history/news knowledge. Layer4 holds current discussion and retrieved past context. Layer5 preserves resumable structured state. Layer6 gives the current agent task and expected output.\n \n The assembly order is eligibility filtering, duplicate removal in compact mode, prioritization, budget accounting, compaction and final constraint reinjection. Baseline preserves original substantive prompt input. Compact can remove repeated paragraphs or shorten older discussion, while retaining symbol, date, price evidence, source IDs and current task. It also requests concise role output to reduce repeated prose passed to later agents. Fresh six-case runs have little past memory, so compact must apply to actual per-agent messages; changing only a memory string would leave the dominant token cost unchanged.\n \n The call budget is configured for the experiment. Per-call maximum output bounds use the provider's existing max_tokens contract. Character estimates may guide context assembly but never replace provider-reported token usage. The model adapter checks before starting a request; a structured-output retry cannot create an extra request after the budget is exhausted. Critical constraints are re-injected after compaction. Factual quality is evaluated independently of brevity.\n \n ## Consequences and reopening conditions\n \n Evidence packs contain prompts and responses and are larger than ordinary reports. Replay is fast because it reconstructs captured state; controlled reruns call the model and remain stochastic. The frozen provider must answer valid parameter variations from data, because an exact tool-transcript lookup would bias the comparison when compact changes tool arguments.\n \n The approval boundary stays outside all model tools. The extension retains responsibility for current-ledger checks even if upstream research changes. Reopen this ADR if an upstream public interface cannot expose a material external read, if multiuser concurrency is added, or if compact cannot satisfy factual constraints without discarding agent roles. No such need justifies silently replacing the baseline.\n+\n+## Affected paths\n+\n+The accepted application scope includes `src/research_desk/config.py`, `graph_adapter.py`, `budget.py`, `evidence.py`, `context.py`, `models.py`, `replay.py`, `report.py`, `cli.py` and the application-owned `src/research_desk/eval/` adapters. `pyproject.toml` exposes the installed extension. These paths implement the already approved evidence, research-context and runtime-budget boundaries. The deterministic approval and ledger changes are specified more precisely in ADR-002. No upstream vendor implementation is replaced.\n",

               "deletions": 0,
               "status": "modified"

               "file": "docs/architecture/adr/003-effective-agent-permissions.md",
               "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/adr/003-effective-agent-permissions.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/adr/003-effective-agent-permissions.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/adr/003-effective-agent-permissions.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,13 @@\n+# ADR-003: Install effective role permissions\n+\n+Status: accepted by leo, 2026-08-31. Requirements: GOV-001 through GOV-004; source: docs/architecture/permission-model.md.\n+\n+The required .opencode/permissions.jsonc is a machine-readable permission manifest. OpenCode does not automatically enforce that filename. The real project opencode.json must load .opencode/rules.md through its documented instructions field and configure supported role permissions. The CI check verifies consistency between the documented manifest and effective configuration.\n+\n+The approved plan/build/verify roles have explicit read/write scope. The implementation role cannot edit rules, approvals or permission decisions. Safety source changes are limited to the existing approved feature/test scope and ADR-002 corrections. Credentials remain outside agent-readable paths. Arbitrary shell execution must not provide an alternative route around frozen-file restrictions; verification commands are separately scoped.\n+\n+This installation is authorized now, but activation waits until the current implementation session ends so it does not unexpectedly revoke an in-progress approved operation. The actual installed configuration and activation evidence are recorded at release. No document claims enforcement before configuration exists.\n+\n+## Affected paths\n+\n+This decision covers `opencode.json`, `.opencode/permissions.jsonc`, `.opencode/rules.md`, `.agent/rules.md` and the permission-consistency checks in `scripts/`. The two rules files and approval records remain owned by leo. This explicit path list documents the same accepted installation scope and does not alter the decision date.\n",

+              "patch": "Index: docs/ci-gates.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/ci-gates.md\t\n+++ docs/ci-gates.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@\n+# Research Desk CI gates\n+\n+Decision owner: leo. The workflow is `.github/workflows/research-desk.yml`. OpenCode generated the check scripts; the coordinating workflow reviewed their behavior against the approved requirements and actual source interfaces. The six independent jobs are intended required checks for the private repository. Server-side branch protection is recorded separately after GitHub accepts or rejects the configuration request.\n+\n+| Gate | Blocking contract | Local command |\n+|---|---|---|\n+| 1. Tests approved before implementation | A scoped approval names the test/plan versions, covers AT-01 through AT-08, and predates implementation. Changed tests need a corresponding approval update. | `python scripts/check_approval.py` |\n+| 2. Static and authority checks | Repository lint, application type checks and dependency consistency succeed. Deterministic policy owners cannot acquire LLM authority. Safety changes carry changed decision evidence. | `python scripts/check_static.py` |\n+| 3. Requirements and traceability | The real YAML registry satisfies its JSON schema; requirement IDs and source/component/test mappings remain consistent. | `python scripts/check_requirements.py` |\n+| 4. Fixed semantic regression | Replay fixed captured packs without networking and exercise the real compact transform on the six fixed source cases. Required facts and tool protocol remain intact. | `python scripts/check_semantic.py` |\n+| 5. Regression | Both the preserved upstream `tests/` suite and application `test/offline/` suite succeed. Live API experiments are recorded separately. | `python scripts/check_regression.py` |\n+| 6. AI-use log | A code or prompt change updates the log with a real session and a scope that covers the changed files. | `python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py` |\n+\n+The workflow uses Python 3.12. Mypy checks `src/research_desk` with imports outside that package skipped; the unchanged upstream project remains covered by its original tests and lint. No gate requires provider credentials. The semantic check measures deterministic input transformation and captured-output replay. The six-case live quality comparison uses separate actual provider calls and saved judgments; its results must not be inferred from an offline CI pass.\n+\n+The scripts accept a repository root and explicit changed-file input for controlled negative demonstrations. PR runs derive the change set from GitHub's base and head revisions. A failed Git query must fail change-dependent gates, and a new branch's all-zero `before` value is handled as the initial tree rather than accepted as a missing ref.\n+\n+## Supervision record\n+\n+The first CI session inspected the actual requirements, approval fields, fixture formats and application declarations. It then repeated baseline verification, so the coordinator interrupted it and sent a shorter implementation directive. The generated first draft had meaningful gaps: an invalid Git diff could appear as no changes, old approval evidence could cover arbitrary future tests, and semantic integration referred to a module that did not exist. These were returned to OpenCode as concrete corrections. The source owner separately received the actual application type findings and fixed them without suppressing the gate.\n+\n+Session: `ses_fa82cafc9ffeeAkOozPwPQ41De`. Raw events and prompts are retained under `transcripts/`; the initial inspection and intervention are part of the record. No source or test files were edited by the CI agent.\n+\n+## Execution evidence\n+\n+Implementation and integration review are in progress. The local six-gate execution, negative examples and final totals will replace this paragraph when those commands finish. This document does not claim a green run or installed branch protection before there is corresponding execution evidence.\n",

+              "file": "docs/process/PROJECT_PLAN.md",
+              "patch": "Index: docs/process/PROJECT_PLAN.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/process/PROJECT_PLAN.md\t\n+++ docs/process/PROJECT_PLAN.md\t\n@@ -1,144 +1,145 @@\n # TradingAgents Research Desk 项目方案\n \n+版本：1.0.0。\n 状态：leo已采纳，OpenCode正在实现。执行来源统一见 `../orchestration/README.md`。本文指标为验收目标，实测结果在后续报告中单列。\n \n ## 一、交付范围\n \n 在现有 TradingAgents 上交付完整流程：**运行研究 → 保存证据包 → 对照研究配置 → 审阅建议 → 确定性策略校验 → 更新模拟账本**。\n \n 第一版使用 CLI 和 HTML/Markdown 报告。只支持 market/news 分析员、US 股票和英语研究报告，仍沿用上游 bull/bear、research manager、trader、risk 与 portfolio manager 流程。完成可演示的纵向切片后再考虑界面美化，不接真实交易。\n \n 这三功能是可实现的起始范围。课程按 N 名组员提出新增需求，当前实际人数未知；后续按真实人数分配有意义的切片，不能把机械拆分当作个人贡献。\n \n ## 二、基线与只读核对结果\n \n 建议固定官方 [TradingAgents v0.4.0](https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents/tree/v0.4.0)，不用滚动 main。已通过 `git ls-remote --tags` 确认标签存在，并下载只读源码到 `/private/tmp/cs5351-tradingagents-v0.4.0`。包版本为0.4.0，要求Python>=3.10。\n \n v0.4.0于2026-08-31发布，包含日期一致性与恢复修复。它是正式标签，但刚发布，不能声称已长期稳定验证；开始实施时跑一次已有离线测试建立本地基线。[官方变更记录](https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents/blob/v0.4.0/CHANGELOG.md)\n \n 已核对的实际接口：\n \n - `TradingAgentsGraph(selected_analysts, debug, config, callbacks)`。\n - `propagate(company_name, trade_date, asset_type=\"stock\")` 返回 `(final_state, signal)`，signal可能为REVIEW。\n - `save_reports(final_state, ticker, save_path=None)` 输出报告。\n - 上游已有结构化输出、decision memory、checkpoint、日期过滤、价格验证、token统计。上述能力都属于继承功能，不能算作本组创新。\n - 实际图止于Portfolio Manager，随后保存状态和决策。对源码的查询未找到独立人工批准状态机或模拟账本；README的模拟执行概述不能代替实现证据。\n \n 保留上游 `tradingagents/`、`cli/` 和 `tests/`。新增模块放 `src/research_desk/`，新增课程测试放 `test/offline/`、`test/live/`，CI同时跑原测试。不要为符合目录树而重写上游代码。\n \n ## 三、新增需求\n \n ### F1：研究证据包与离线复现\n \n 保存分析日期、股票、模型/配置、prompt版本、实际输入资料、LLM请求/结果/usage、报告、决策及本次用到的记忆。导出资料包并生成来源索引。\n \n 离线复现读取已捕获状态与事件，重建报告和模拟策略结果，完全不调用网络。受控重跑则用冻结资料再次调用LLM，供比较配置；LLM的输出仍可能变化，两种功能需要明确区分。\n \n | ID | 优先级 | 需求与fit criterion |\n |---|---|---|\n | FR-001 | Must | 一条命令导出完整证据包，新进程可导入并重建报告；列出所有实际调用和运行配置 |\n | NFR-001 | Must | 固定6包离线复现成功率100%，外部调用数0，结构化决策/策略结果相同；本机单包重建<2秒 |\n | SEC-001 | Must | 输出不包含API凭证；所有未来才可用的资料不得用于声明为历史评估的研究 |\n \n 报告生成时间等展示元数据不参与一致性判断。文件摘要仅用于完整性，不充当用户版本号。上游已有价格snapshot；增量是跨输入、运行和结果的可移交证据包。\n \n ### F2：人工批准的模拟账本\n \n 研究结束产生待审阅建议。操作员选择股数并批准，系统根据当前账本、冻结价格与策略判断是否允许模拟执行。状态为 `PENDING_REVIEW → APPROVED/REJECTED → SIMULATED/REVIEW_REQUIRED`。Hold或REVIEW不产生交易。\n \n 初版教学策略：现金USD100000、仅整股、禁止卖空、买入后单股票市值<=组合权益10%。批准绑定具体建议版本，执行前重查当前账本；重复执行同一批准不会重复记账。模型只建议方向和解释，不能设定政策、批准者或余额。\n \n | ID | 优先级 | 需求与fit criterion |\n |---|---|---|\n | FR-002 | Must | 用户可列出建议、看证据、批准/拒绝，观察账本和状态变化 |\n | NFR-002 | Must | 固定允许/拒绝/重复执行案例100%符合策略，策略裁决不调用LLM |\n | INV-001 | Must | 每项账本变化引用已批准建议版本及通过的确定性策略结果；违规次数0 |\n | INV-002 | Must | 未批准、上游REVIEW、资金/持仓不足、超限或价格缺失时不得改变账本；逃逸次数0 |\n \n 操作员直接调用review命令，记录实际本机操作者；研究LLM不能调用review或账本工具。第一版是单机个人工作台，不声称实现企业身份认证。安全失败返回明确的REVIEW_REQUIRED或业务拒绝，并保留账本原状态。\n \n ### F3：紧凑上下文与成本对照\n \n 增加研究调用预算、上下文装配和baseline/compact成对比较。保留股票身份、研究日期、关键价格、站立约束和当前任务；去重重复报告，压缩较旧讨论；压缩后重新加入关键约束。\n \n | ID | 优先级 | 需求与fit criterion |\n |---|---|---|\n | FR-003 | Must | 同一固定资料集输出两种配置的质量、调用数、input/output tokens、wall time和停止原因 |\n | NFR-003 | Must | 达到配置的调用数上限后不开始下一次LLM请求；预算停止结果不可进入可批准建议 |\n | QUALITY-001 | Must | 固定6组资料的强制事实字段正确率100%，引用有效率>=95%，支持度与相关性均>=0.8 |\n | COST-001 | Should | 同模型/资料/范围下compact总tokens降低>=20%，质量平均下降<=0.05 |\n | PERF-001 | Should | compact总wall time不高于baseline的110%，完整报告重试和所有样本 |\n \n 复用上游 `max_tokens` 作为每次输出上限，不另造同名配置。总token必须记录真实usage；不声称不同网关下有精确美元硬上限。2组资料用于开发，另4组在开发前冻结；最终完整跑两种配置各6组。引用、评分和应用token分开记录，避免评估费用被隐藏。\n \n MoSCoW取舍：先保证完整工作流和Must项，成本/性能提升有真实比较后才认定达成；图形界面、更多分析员、并行批处理和券商接入不进入第一版。\n \n ## 四、最小架构\n \n | 新模块 | 责任 | 复用点 |\n |---|---|---|\n | `research.py` | 研究生命周期和RunRecord | TradingAgentsGraph、配置、报告 |\n | `evidence.py` | 调用/输入记录、资料包、离线复现 | callbacks、现有报告写入器 |\n | `context.py` | 选择、去重、压缩、重注入关键约束 | 实际prompt所有者的局部接入 |\n | `budget.py` | 调用预算与实际usage | StatsCallbackHandler的计量方式、上游max_tokens |\n | `review.py` | 批准状态、策略、账本事务 | 最终signal仅作建议输入 |\n | `cli.py` | analyze/export/replay/compare/review命令 | 既有typer/rich |\n \n 新字段显式用已有Pydantic声明；新状态用项目SQLite数据库和运行目录。模拟账本与上游研究记忆分开。第一版顺序执行分析，避免上游进程级配置在并发任务中混用。\n \n callbacks不能自动覆盖全部外部数据：identity、回报读取等存在直接数据路径。OpenCode必须先定位这些真实边界，再提出最小接口扩展。禁止全局monkeypatch，禁止在共享vendor路由里按项目名加分支。\n \n 候选A：全面改图；候选B：应用层加必要的窄接口；候选C：重写多agent。选择B以控制变更范围，保留上游成熟能力和可比较基线。若真实接入限制阻碍证据完整性，则针对具体接口重开ADR。\n \n ```mermaid\n flowchart LR\n     U[操作员] --> C[CLI]\n     C --> R[研究编排]\n     R --> X[上下文与预算]\n     X --> T[TradingAgents / DeepSeek]\n     T --> E[证据包]\n     E --> F[复现与对照报告]\n     E --> P[待审阅建议]\n     U --> A[人工批准]\n     A --> P\n     P --> G[确定性策略]\n     G --> L[模拟账本]\n ```\n \n 记忆设计：记录原始资料、结构化研究结果和模拟账本；每次运行冻结实际使用的上游记忆。先支持同一应用版本恢复，数据schema使用单一语义版本字段；真实格式变化才添加迁移。运行证据保留到课程验收后，删除策略由学生决定；凭证不入库。\n \n ## 五、实施切片\n \n 1. 固定版本、许可与继承需求，建立已有测试基线。\n 2. leo采纳 `APPROVAL_PACKET.md` 与 `TEST_PLAN.md`；OpenCode给出精确文件/接口计划后按既定方案实施。\n 3. 用离线fixture完成证据→建议→review→账本，展示一个批准和一个拒绝案例。\n 4. 接入一次真实DeepSeek研究，生成完整证据包，记录实际usage。\n 5. 接入compact与预算，完成固定的成对质量/成本比较。\n 6. 接通课程六门禁。先完成本地机制，再通过已确认可用的GitHub账户配置私有仓库、required checks与branch protection，展示失败PR及修正结果。\n 7. 冻结交付，生成报告、ZIP与10分钟演示。会话和干预记录在真实发生时保存，不事后编造。\n \n 每个切片围绕正常路径和必要的负面案例验证，不为内部每个函数补镜像测试，不先投入无关重构或前端。\n \n ##
