The extension retains responsibility for current-ledger checks even if upstream research changes. Reopen this ADR if an upstream public interface cannot expose a material external read, if multiuser concurrency is added, or if compact cannot satisfy factual constraints without discarding agent roles. The concrete plan and tests were approved at 12:05:17.791955 UTC before OpenCode's first implementation event at 12:06:32.695 UTC.\\\\n4: \\\\n5: ## Context and alternatives\\\\n6: \\\\n7: TradingAgents v0.4.0 already provides multi-agent research, structured decisions, date-aware memory, checkpointing and price validation. The missing product workflow is portable evidence followed by explicit approval and paper execution. A complete graph rewrite would discard tested domain behavior and make the optimization baseline incomparable. Editing every upstream prompt and tool would distribute application-specific policy across many owners. A narrow application extension keeps the experimental boundary visible.\\\\n8: \\\\n9: Candidate A modifies the entire graph and shared vendors. Candidate B subclasses/composes the existing graph and implements policy outside it. Candidate C builds a small new agent demo. The evaluation table selects B because it preserves genuine AI integration while keeping deterministic authority isolated. The original graph's full selected role sequence is retained in both experimental arms.\\\\n10: \\\\n11: ## Context layers and assembly\\\\n12: \\\\n13: Layer1 identifies the instrument and analysis cutoff. Layer2 states standing constraints: use available evidence, retain source identity, distinguish unknown facts and keep execution advisory. Layer3 supplies frozen market/history/news knowledge. Layer4 holds current discussion and retrieved past context. Layer5 preserves resumable structured state. Layer6 gives the current agent task and expected output.\\\\n14: \\\\n15: The assembly order is eligibility filtering, duplicate removal in compact mode, prioritization, budget accounting, compaction and final constraint reinjection. Baseline preserves original substantive prompt input. Compact can remove repeated paragraphs or shorten older discussion, while retaining symbol, date, price evidence, source IDs and current task. It also requests concise role output to reduce repeated prose passed to later agents. Fresh six-case runs have little past memory, so compact must apply to actual per-agent messages; changing only a memory string would leave the dominant token cost unchanged.\\\\n16: \\\\n17: The call budget is configured for the experiment. Per-call maximum output bounds use the provider's existing max_tokens contract. Character estimates may guide context assembly but never replace provider-reported token usage. The model adapter checks before starting a request; a structured-output retry cannot create an extra request after the budget is exhausted. Critical constraints are re-injected after compaction. Factual quality is evaluated independently of brevity.\\\\n18: \\\\n19: ## Consequences and reopening conditions\\\\n20: \\\\n21: Evidence packs contain prompts and responses and are larger than ordinary reports. Replay is fast because it reconstructs captured state; controlled reruns call the model and remain stochastic. The frozen provider must answer valid parameter variations from data, because an exact tool-transcript lookup would bias the comparison when compact changes tool arguments.\\\\n22: \\\\n23: The approval boundary stays outside all model tools. The extension retains responsibility for current-ledger checks even if upstream research changes. Reopen this ADR if an upstream public interface cannot expose a material external read, if multiuser concurrency is added, or if compact cannot satisfy factual constraints without discarding agent roles. No such need justifies silently replacing the baseline.\\\\n\\\\n(End of file - total 23 lines)\\\\n</content>\\\",\\\"metadata\\\":{\\\"preview\\\":\\\"# ADR-001: Extend the existing graph through application-owned seams\\\\n\\\\nStatus: accepted by leo, 2026-08-31. By deploying specialized LLM-powered agents: from fundamental analysts, sentiment experts, and technical analysts, to trader, risk management team, the platform collaboratively evaluates market conditions and informs trading decisions. Moreover, these agents engage in dynamic discussions to pinpoint the optimal strategy.\\n-\\n-<p align=\\\"center\\\">\\n-  <img src=\\\"assets/schema.png\\\" style=\\\"width: 100%; height: auto;\\\">\\n-</p>\\n-\\n-> TradingAgents framework is designed for research purposes. [It is not intended as financial, investment, or trading advice.](https://tauric.ai/disclaimer/)\\n-\\n-Our framework decomposes complex trading tasks into specialized roles.\\n-\\n-### Analyst Team\\n-- Fundamentals Analyst: Evaluates company financials and performance metrics, identifying intrinsic values and potential red flags.\\n-- Sentiment Analyst: Aggregates news headlines, StockTwits, and Reddit chatter into a single sentiment read to gauge short-term market mood.\\n-- News Analyst: Monitors global news and macroeconomic indicators, interpreting the impact of events on market conditions.\\n-- Technical Analyst: Utilizes technical indicators (like MACD and RSI) to detect trading patterns and forecast price movements.\\n-\\n-<p align=\\\"center\\\">\\n-  <img src=\\\"assets/analyst.png\\\" width=\\\"100%\\\" style=\\\"display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;\\\">\\n-</p>\\n-\\n-### Researcher Team\\n-- Comprises both bullish and bearish researchers who critically assess the insights provided by the Analyst Team. Participant and evaluation identifier: **leo**. Relative contribution: **1.0**. The implementation extends official TradingAgents **v0.4.0**. Repository: [Fighterforever/cs5351-tradingagents-research-desk](https://github.com/Fighterforever/cs5351-tradingagents-research-desk), private.\\\\n+\\\\n+This project uses a genuine language-model research graph to investigate a practical software engineering question: how can a user inspect the evidence behind an AI recommendation, reproduce its presentation, and control the consequences of accepting it? The delivered workflow connects research to a portable evidence package, then to an explicitly approved paper transaction. A second workflow compares the cost and quality of two context strategies using the same underlying research system.\\\\n+\\\\n+The project was conducted as a teaching evaluation under the identifier leo. The user authorized autonomous decisions and DeepSeek API execution. OpenCode generated application, test and CI code; the coordinating workflow supplied bounded prompts, reviewed declared contracts, executed experiments and prepared documentation. This provenance statement applies to the decision and reflection records throughout the project. No additional students or university student numbers are invented. The repository preserves the real OpenCode sessions and intervention records.\\\\n+\\\\n+The report distinguishes the system's research capability from the authority to change paper state. Research can produce useful reasoning while still being uncertain or incomplete. Execution requires an exact approval and a deterministic policy result. The experiment likewise separates measured token reduction from factual quality. A shorter report earns no quality credit simply because it costs less to generate.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 1. Problem, scope and contribution\\\\n+\\\\n+TradingAgents is a substantial existing multi-agent application. It already separates research perspectives, produces structured decisions and retains research memory. Its reports are valuable to a reader, but an engineering assessment needs additional evidence about how a particular report was produced and what an application may do with it. A saved report alone does not identify every material input or establish that a later action followed the user's approval.\\\\n+\\\\n+Research Desk adds three cohesive features. The first captures a run as a transferable evidence package and reconstructs the report in a new process without external calls. The second turns a completed recommendation into an operator-reviewed proposal and applies a paper transaction only after deterministic checks. The third adds context and request-budget controls, then measures a baseline/compact comparison over six fixed cases. Each feature participates in an end-to-end user workflow rather than existing as an isolated demonstration.\\\\n+\\\\n+The first feature answers the operator's question, “What did this run actually see?” Its package records instrument identity, analysis cutoff, material tool inputs, model requests, model responses and terminal state. Actual provider usage accompanies the calls. The package can be exported as a ZIP and inspected on another machine. The replay path reconstructs saved results, so it has no reason to instantiate a model client. A controlled rerun has a different purpose: it executes the research graph again against the same frozen data, allowing an experiment on context strategy.\\\\n+\\\\n+The second feature answers, “Which action did I approve?” A proposal includes the research evidence reference, direction, price and operator-selected quantity. Approval refers to exact terms. If those terms change, the old approval cannot authorize the new proposal. The policy checks the current ledger at execution time because the user's earlier review cannot freeze cash or holdings indefinitely. Repeating an already completed execution returns the original transaction instead of applying a second financial side effect.\\\\n+\\\\n+The third feature asks whether repeated prompt material can be reduced without damaging evidence-grounded research. The complete selected upstream graph remains in place for both arms. The same DeepSeek model and inference settings are used. The source corpus is fixed before the comparison. Actual token usage supplies the cost measure, while an independent assessment supplies the quality measure. The request budget also provides a concrete degraded-mode behavior: a stopped research run remains inspectable but does not create an approvable recommendation.\\\\n+\\\\n+The scope deliberately fits a single local operator. The application handles US equities with the market and news analysts, retains the downstream researcher/trader/risk roles, and produces English reports. It offers CLI commands and readable report artifacts. It has no broker integration and places no real orders. This boundary makes the safety requirement testable without presenting a classroom paper ledger as a production trading platform.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 2. Existing-system analysis and baseline selection\\\\n+\\\\n+The baseline is the official v0.4.0 tag from TauricResearch/TradingAgents. The tag was verified in the public repository, and its source was copied into the project before extension work. The release was new on the execution date. The project therefore uses a formal pinned version and establishes a local test baseline instead of describing the release as proven by a long operational history.\\\\n+\\\\n+Source analysis identified the actual extension contracts. TradingAgentsGraph accepts selected analysts, configuration and callbacks. Its propagation path returns a terminal graph state and a signal. The report writer consumes that saved state. Instrument resolution and returns reads include direct data paths that are not ordinary model tool calls. The dependency declarations and provider adapters were also examined before selecting how the extension would access DeepSeek.\\\\n+\\\\n+This inspection prevented several false novelty claims. Structured decisions are inherited. Date-aware memory is inherited. Checkpoint and resume behavior is inherited. The verified market snapshot and token-statistics pattern also belong to the upstream project. Research Desk's contribution is the integrated evidence/review/evaluation workflow around those capabilities. The requirements registry lists inherited requirements with source links so a reviewer can distinguish reuse from new behavior.\\\\n+\\\\n+The unmodified upstream test run completed with **649 passed, 2 skipped and 71 subtests passed**. The saved log records the invocation and result. The skips concerned an optional AWS dependency and a live DeepSeek integration test that was not given a key in that baseline invocation. The extension retains the full original tests directory. Later regression checks run both the upstream suite and the additional application tests.\\\\n+\\\\n+The repository layout preserves upstream source and licensing. New application modules live under src/research_desk. New deterministic tests live under test/offline, and API-dependent experiment assets are separated from them. The Python environment belongs to this project. Installing its dependencies does not change the environment used for the separate course assignments. This isolation matters because dependency changes can otherwise create failures in work that the project did not modify.\\\\n+\\\\n+A real extension also needs to be installable. The first generated slice created its modules but initially omitted the necessary src-layout package-discovery configuration. The CLI then failed to import the package. OpenCode corrected pyproject.toml, after which the installed research-desk command ran successfully. This was an integration defect with a clear reproduction, not a reason to replace the application with a standalone script that bypassed packaging.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 3. Requirements engineering and acceptance strategy\\\\n+\\\\n+The machine-readable product requirements document identifies the user, scope and three features. A consolidated registry contains 23 requirements. Each entry has an identifier, type, statement, priority and a fit criterion expressed as a metric, comparison operator, threshold and verification method. Source links identify inherited behavior. Component and test references make the registry useful to implementation and CI rather than merely readable prose.\\\\n+\\\\n+The priorities follow MoSCoW. Correct evidence handling, deterministic authority and complete measurement are Must requirements. A20% token reduction and a compact wall time within110% of baseline are Should targets. This distinction establishes a decision rule before observing results. A measured optimization can miss its target without justifying a weaker approval boundary. Conversely, a passing safety test cannot be used as evidence that the context strategy saved tokens.\\\\n+\\\\n+The strongest invariants have zero-tolerance fit criteria. Every ledger mutation must refer to exact approved terms and passing current-state policy checks. An unapproved, rejected, nontradeable or policy-violating proposal must leave the ledger unchanged. The graph must not gain execution authority from text in a report. No request may begin after the configured call limit. These are operational rules with observable failure behavior, not broad aspirations such as “the system should be safe.”\\\\n+\\\\n+The fixed teaching policy starts with USD100000 cash. Quantities are positive whole shares. Shorting is forbidden. A purchase may not leave one stock above10% of portfolio equity. The price comes from research evidence; the operator cannot type a favorable execution price. The operator chooses quantity and approves it. A valid sell can reduce an owned position, while a sell beyond the holding is rejected. Hold and REVIEW do not produce a tradeable proposal.\\\\n+\\\\n+Eight acceptance specifications cover the important behavior. AT-01 exports and replays a complete package in a new process, then tests an incomplete package. AT-02 checks source availability, cutoff dates and duplicate handling. AT-03 demonstrates a valid approved transaction and repeat execution. AT-04 covers the forbidden execution cases. AT-05 changes approved terms or current portfolio state before execution. AT-06 exercises the actual request limit and critical context preservation. AT-07 compares six paired research runs. AT-08 exercises the six CI gates and their failure paths.\\\\n+\\\\n+The plan and test specifications were approved at **2026-08-31 12:05:17.791955 UTC**. The first recorded OpenCode implementation event occurred at **12:06:32.695 UTC**. The approval file and raw session provide the chronology. A CI gate must validate the dates and referenced tests rather than treating a freely editable APPROVED string as sufficient evidence. The scope of that decision is the three-feature project, not an indefinite authorization to change any future policy.\\\\n+\\\\n+The most useful negative cases correspond to plausible business failures. For example, approving100 shares at USD100 in an empty USD100000 account reaches the cap exactly. An order for101 shares must fail. However, those two tests alone cannot establish a total-position invariant. The review therefore adds a purchase after an existing position. That example distinguishes a correct holdings cap from an implementation that limits only the latest ticket.\\\\n+\\\\n+Requirement volatility was controlled by keeping the feature scope fixed while clarifying ambiguous semantics. The project did not add a web application, extra analyst families or brokerage integration during implementation. The significant clarifications were that no-shorting permits valid sales, the cap applies to total holdings, approval includes quantity and evidence identity, and compact must affect actual per-agent inputs. Those clarifications are recorded in ADR-002 and the defect diary. They arose from reading the implementation against the approved behavior.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 4. Architecture and authority boundaries\\\\n+\\\\n+The selected architecture adds application-owned seams around the real graph. Three candidates were compared: broad modification of upstream internals, an application extension, and a replacement demonstration graph. The evaluation considered preservation of baseline behavior, deterministic authority, evidence coverage, delivery scope and maintenance. The application extension received the strongest design score because it preserves the real AI system while keeping the new transaction policy outside it.\\\\n+\\\\n+The architecture has a clear flow. The operator invokes the CLI. ResearchRunner assembles a configured graph and a run recorder. The graph consumes market/news evidence and produces research state. EvidencePackIO saves the material needed for inspection and replay. A completed tradeable result can create a pending proposal. The operator reviews exact terms. Policy evaluates the current ledger. Storage applies a permitted transaction atomically and records its provenance.\\\\n+\\\\n+```mermaid\\\\n+flowchart TD\\\\n+    A[Operator request] --> B[ResearchRunner]\\\\n+    C[Frozen identity, prices and news] --> B\\\\n+    B --> D[Real TradingAgents graph]\\\\n+    D --> E[Requests, responses, usage and final state]\\\\n+    E --> F[Portable evidence package]\\\\n+    F --> G[Zero-network report replay]\\\\n+    F --> H[Pending proposal]\\\\n+    I[Operator exact-term approval] --> H\\\\n+    H --> J[Current-ledger policy]\\\\n+    J --> K[Paper transaction]\\\\n+```\\\\n+\\\\n+Module ownership follows these responsibilities. Models declares the persistent records. Config owns settings and teaching constants. Evidence captures calls and packages them. Graph_adapter owns the narrow integration with upstream. Context owns assembly and compaction. Budget owns request accounting. Review owns proposal transitions, while policy owns deterministic business decisions. Storage owns SQLite persistence. Replay reconstructs saved outputs, and the CLI exposes these capabilities to the operator.\\\\n+\\\\n+The distinction between policy and storage is important. Policy decides whether the proposed state change is permitted. Storage records that approved change and its result. Neither module asks a model for permission. The graph's available tools contain research capabilities, and no tool grants approval or mutates the ledger. A sentence inside a model report requesting a policy bypass remains text; it is never interpreted as an operator command.\\\\n+\\\\n+Approval refers to exact content. A fingerprint is appropriate for this purpose because it detects a changed combination of material evidence and trade terms. The fingerprint does not replace ordinary release or schema versions. After approval, changing quantity or price requires another review. A transaction also rechecks current cash and holdings because an earlier approved action may have changed the portfolio. These checks protect different boundaries: exact-content binding protects the user's decision, and current-state evaluation protects the portfolio invariant.\\\\n+\\\\n+The REVIEW_REQUIRED state is recoverable. The first implementation correctly refused an unapproved execution but then prevented approval after entering the recovery state. That would leave the operator with a safe failure and no practical path forward. The corrected state machine allows the operator to inspect and approve the current terms. Completed and rejected proposals retain their explicit business meaning. The state-machine tests cover recovery rather than merely asserting that an error occurs.\\\\n+\\\\n+Research and ledger memory have separate purposes. Upstream memory supports reflection on earlier decisions. The paper ledger represents approved positions and cash. Capturing the memory used in a research run makes that run inspectable, but a memory entry cannot authorize a transaction. Each evaluation process uses its own application home so experimental state cannot leak between cases. The application does not claim multiuser service semantics; its supported workflow is a single operator using a local CLI.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 5. Evidence capture, replay and fixed inputs\\\\n+\\\\n+Evidence capture begins at the real boundaries of the system. Model callbacks can record messages, returned content and reported usage. Tool callbacks can capture arguments and results. They do not automatically observe every data read. Source inspection identified identity resolution and return-history paths that bypass ordinary tool calls. The application subclass explicitly records or freezes these paths, closing a material gap in evidence completeness.\\\\n+\\\\n+A package contains a manifest, material input snapshot, event stream, call records, usage summary and terminal state. It can include the proposal and presentation metadata. Completion is a structural claim about required records being present and parseable. A package missing a required record must fail replay rather than silently inventing it. Failed research still retains diagnostic evidence, but its incomplete status cannot become an approved recommendation.\\\\n+\\\\n+Replay reads saved state and reconstructs the reports and structured decision. It does not ask a language model to recreate previous prose. The same package therefore gives an inspectable report even when the API is unavailable. Display timestamps may differ because they describe the reconstruction, while the decision and policy-relevant fields remain stable. The acceptance test starts replay in a fresh process and blocks external access to establish the intended dependency boundary.\\\\n+\\\\n+A controlled rerun has a different contract. It executes the full research graph again, using fixed non-LLM data. Different context may lead the model to request a different indicator window or select a different valid tool argument. An exact lookup table of old tool calls would answer only the original transcript and return missing data for another valid request. That behavior could confound the comparison. The fixed-data adapter therefore derives valid responses from the same underlying market CSV and source corpus.\\\\n+\\\\n+The experiment uses six real equity cases. Prices were retrieved from Yahoo Finance through the installed yfinance library and saved as CSV. Source manifests record retrieval time, row count and latest eligible trading date. Official issuer releases provide the news facts. Availability is tied to the issuer's publication date, not the later retrieval timestamp. The inputs were frozen before final comparison and are preserved with their source identities.\\\\n+\\\\n+| Case | Analysis date | Frozen close, USD | Role in experiment |\\\\n+|---|---|---:|---|\\\\n+| AAPL |2026-07-31|308.9100036621094|Development|\\\\n+| MSFT |2026-07-30|451.1000061035156|Development|\\\\n+| NVDA |2026-08-27|227.97999572753906|Held out|\\\\n+| AMZN |2026-07-31|271.5799865722656|Held out|\\\\n+| META |2026-07-30|539.030029296875|Held out|\\\\n+| GOOGL |2026-07-23|317.69000244140625|Held out|\\\\n+\\\\n+The cases include facts that require careful interpretation. Amazon's reported net income includes a substantial other-income component associated primarily with Anthropic. Alphabet's net income includes large unrealized equity gains. Apple's reported margin and earnings include a tariff-refund effect. Microsoft's release distinguishes GAAP and non-GAAP earnings. These features make factual support more meaningful than a check that a report merely contains the right ticker.\\\\n+\\\\n+The market files remain actual observations. Optional macroeconomic or prediction-market information absent from the fixed corpus receives an explicit unavailable response. The adapter must not fabricate a convenient value to keep a role busy. An unavailable source can be discussed as missing evidence, and the resulting report should state what can be concluded from the information supplied. The model's reasoning does not change the provenance of its inputs.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 6. Context engineering and request budgets\\\\n+\\\\n+The context design has six layers. Instrument identity establishes the subject. Standing constraints establish the analysis cutoff and advisory boundary. Retrieved knowledge supplies market and news evidence. Conversation history carries earlier arguments. Structured state supports continuation. The current task tells a specific role what it must produce. These layers are explicit because compression should remove redundancy without losing the task's controlling facts.\\\\n+\\\\n+The assembly pipeline first filters evidence for eligibility. It then removes repeated material in compact mode, prioritizes essential content and applies a context budget. After compaction, it re-injects critical constraints. Symbol, analysis date, evidence price, source identity and the current task remain visible. Older discussion may be shortened when it repeats facts already present. The compact strategy also requests concise role responses to reduce repeated prose propagated to later roles.\\\\n+\\\\n+Baseline preserves the original substantive input and follows the same graph. It is not padded with duplicate text to manufacture a favorable comparison. Compact retains all selected roles and uses the same model settings. The comparison therefore measures a context strategy rather than an architectural reduction in work. Both the input and output sides of provider usage are reported because concise output can affect later input size as well as the current response.\\\\n+\\\\n+The first generated context implementation focused on past memory. That was a plausible local interpretation of compaction, and its unit tests could demonstrate deduplication. It would provide little benefit in six fresh cases with little memory. The review identified this mismatch before claiming an improvement and directed OpenCode to transform actual per-agent messages. This intervention illustrates why workload analysis matters: a correct local utility can fail to address the dominant cost of the application.\\\\n+\\\\n+The request budget is an operational constraint. The counter must be checked before a real request starts. Merely recording an exceeded budget after a response would still spend the next call. Callback behavior also matters because some frameworks swallow callback exceptions, and structured-output fallbacks may retry a failed call. The acceptance test therefore exercises the invocation boundary with a fake provider and attempts one call beyond the configured limit.\\\\n+\\\\n+A budget-stopped run keeps the evidence collected so far and records a distinct terminal outcome. It does not claim completion and does not create a tradeable proposal. A legitimate run that completes on its final allowed call should remain completed; reaching the numeric limit alone is not proof that another request was blocked. This distinction makes stop reasons useful for both the user and the evaluation.\\\\n+\\\\n+Per-call output limits use the actual provider contract. The project does not treat a rough character-to-token estimate as measured API usage. Character estimates can help select context, but the report's cost comparison comes from actual usage metadata. Judge calls are separately recorded. A reduction in application tokens is therefore not inflated by omitting the cost of quality evaluation from the evidence record.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 7. Verification results and experimental method\\\\n+\\\\n+Verification has three tiers. Structural checks cover installation, module contracts, permissions, requirement schema and static analysis. Regression checks run all earlier test suites. Behavioral checks exercise the approval boundary, evidence replay and research quality. These tiers are complementary. An importable package can still have an incorrect holdings cap, and a passing deterministic ledger test says nothing about whether a research report faithfully cites earnings evidence.\\\\n+\\\\n+The first extension slice converged to **47 passing offline tests**. The saved OpenCode session contains the real failures and fixes. The tests cover the CLI workflow, incomplete package rejection, point-in-time context, approval, denial and recovery. Review after this checkpoint found omitted business semantics and an incomplete experimental adapter. Those findings triggered a focused second implementation round rather than a claim that47 tests established final acceptance.\\\\n+\\\\n+A demonstration fixture uses a USD100 evidence price and a USD100000 initial account. It is intentionally constructed and identified as a fixture. The recorded CLI workflow first rejects execution without approval. After leo approves100 shares, execution leaves USD90000 cash and100 shares. Repeating the execution returns the same transaction and leaves cash unchanged. A separate101-share example fails the10% cap and preserves the original ledger. These commands establish the user-visible workflow without presenting the fixture price as a live market quote.\\\\n+\\\\n+The fixed research experiment contains12 application runs: six cases under baseline and six under compact. AAPL and MSFT are the development cases. NVDA, AMZN, META and GOOGL were reserved before final tuning. The same frozen inputs, complete selected graph, DeepSeek model and inference configuration apply to both arms. Each case has a saved outcome, call count, input tokens, output tokens and measured elapsed time. Independent OS processes may run concurrently, but cases do not share application state.\\\\n+\\\\n+The quality method has deterministic and semantic parts. Identity, analysis date, captured price and recommendation state are checked against the package. Source references must correspond to available corpus evidence. An independent live judge assesses support and relevance using the predeclared rubric, with the same procedure for both arms. A support score of0.8 requires adequately supported main conclusions without a critical fabrication. A relevance score of0.8 requires the core stock/date task to be covered with limited irrelevant material.\\\\n+\\\\n+Citation validity requires a source to support the associated claim, not merely an existing source identifier. Uncited factual claims are reported so that a model cannot improve the citation percentage by deleting citations. The judge receives the fixed evidence and report content, and its raw response remains available. A malformed judgment is an evaluation failure requiring an explicit recovery record. It is never replaced with an invented perfect score.\\\\n+\\\\n+[[LIVE_RESULTS]]\\\\n+\\\\n+The Should targets are evaluated against the saved runs. Total token reduction is one minus compact application tokens divided by baseline application tokens. Quality retention compares the two arms' mean scores, with a maximum permitted decline of0.05. The wall-time ratio compares measured elapsed time under the disclosed execution conditions. Failures and retries remain in the experiment history. Results from a repaired development run do not justify quietly discarding an unfavorable held-out case.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 8. Coding governance, CI and repository evidence\\\\n+\\\\n+AGENTS.md is the single entry point for coding work. It identifies the baseline, reading order, module ownership and verification requirements. Prompt.md asks the coding agent for a concrete plan before code generation and requires a matching approval. Current approval authorizes the recorded scope. Future safety changes require a new ADR and a specific decision. Rules and approval records are owned by leo rather than by the implementation role.\\\\n+\\\\n+The permission model separates planning, building, verification and release. Planning reads requirements and declared interfaces. Building writes approved application and test paths. Verification reads source and evidence and writes results. Release packages reviewed artifacts and uses the authorized private remote. None of these roles needs to read global credential files. The host injects runtime credentials only into the appropriate child process, and they are excluded from saved evidence and submission artifacts.\\\\n+\\\\n+The first five inherited capabilities remain covered by the original regression suite. New acceptance tests map through the requirement trace matrix to their enforcing component and runtime record. Each safety invariant has a concrete fallback: unchanged ledger, explicit rejection, REVIEW_REQUIRED, or an incomplete research state. The project records such outcomes so a reviewer can diagnose why an action stopped rather than seeing an undifferentiated error.\\\\n+\\\\n+The CI design implements six gates. The first validates test approval and chronology. The second runs lint, type and dependency checks and adds checks for safety-relevant changes. The third validates the requirements registry against its schema. The fourth re-evaluates fixed captured evidence against semantic properties for prompt/model changes. The fifth runs all prior regressions. The sixth requires the AI-use log to change when code or prompts change. Negative examples and repaired outcomes provide evidence that these checks can actually reject a change.\\\\n+\\\\n+An offline semantic replay gate has a precise scope. It can recompute factual and structural properties of committed captured outputs. It cannot establish the quality of a newly generated live answer without calling the model. The release evidence therefore includes the actual paired live evaluation as a separate artifact. The project does not rename a deterministic fixture assertion as a fresh language-model judgment.\\\\n+\\\\n+[[GITHUB_RESULTS]]\\\\n+\\\\n+The repository remains private. The original public repository is retained as upstream, and the private course repository is origin. No changes are pushed to TauricResearch. Source history begins from the real upstream baseline and records the extension with concise meaningful commits. The README explains purpose, architecture, setup and test commands, and links to the real GitHub project. Local check success and server-enforced branch protection are recorded separately.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 9. Supervised process and improvements\\\\n+\\\\n+The process began with course-document analysis and existing-source inspection. Requirements and acceptance examples were written before implementation. The initial approved slice connected evidence, review and a paper ledger so there was an early end-to-end workflow. This reduced integration uncertainty before adding the live experiment. The project then used measured failures and code review to choose the next changes.\\\\n+\\\\n+OpenCode's first session generated the application and tests. Its raw record includes implementation attempts, test failures and corrections. The coordinating review examined business contracts instead of relying entirely on the agent's success statement. The review caught the difference between a ticket cap and total holdings, the omission of shares from approval binding, and the unintended rejection of all sales. It also noticed that an empty-memory compaction example could pass while delivering no useful savings on the planned workload.\\\\n+\\\\n+The first session continued cleanup after its offline milestone. The coordinator ended that session and opened a shorter, focused live-evaluation session. This preserved the useful source changes and reduced the cost of repeatedly carrying a large context. The second prompt named the precise defects, fixed corpus, adapter behavior and required live commands. It did not ask the agent to revisit the entire project or produce another broad plan.\\\\n+\\\\n+Work was divided by ownership to avoid conflicting edits. The core OpenCode session handled application and tests. A separate OpenCode session handled CI scripts and schema. Documentation was maintained alongside the source, and a video workflow captured actual CLI commands in an isolated demo home. The remote repository work waited for a concrete local deliverable. This parallel structure used the API waiting time productively while keeping each code owner bounded.\\\\n+\\\\n+Defect trends are described from actual observations rather than invented issue counts. Early failures concerned packaging, context bookkeeping and a recovery transition. Later review findings concerned business semantics and experimental validity. That progression suggests the implementation became mechanically runnable before it fully represented the approved contracts. The improvement was to move from broad test counts to a smaller number of discriminating examples at each authority boundary.\\\\n+\\\\n+Ambiguity resolution is explicit. “No shorting” was interpreted as allowing a sell up to owned shares. “Ten percent position” refers to resulting holdings. “Approval” covers quantity and material evidence. “Replay” reconstructs a saved result, while “rerun” regenerates one from fixed input. “Token reduction” refers to actual provider usage. These definitions are reflected in the requirements, ADRs and tests so later maintenance does not have to reconstruct the reasoning from a conversation.\\\\n+\\\\n+Artifacts co-evolved through the trace matrix. A change to the holdings interpretation affected the policy owner, approval decision, test examples and defect diary. A change to the context strategy affected ADR-001, the runtime adapter and evaluation method. The schema correction made the machine-readable registry validate the document actually committed, rather than an unrelated example record. The AI-use log points to real sessions and their scopes. No artifact is considered complete merely because its filename matches the course checklist.\\\\n+\\\\n+The project also separates review authority from outcome evidence. A decision can authorize a plan, but it cannot declare an unrun test successful. An ADR can select an architecture, but it cannot establish measured token savings. A workflow file can define checks, but it cannot prove a server rejected a merge. This separation made the final deliverable more reviewable and prevented documentation from outrunning implementation.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 10. Limitations and remaining risks\\\\n+\\\\n+The application is a local teaching research desk. Its approval identity is the local operator identifier and does not provide enterprise authentication. It does not connect to a broker or model real execution costs. Portfolio valuation uses the documented evidence/mark convention, and the workload does not establish multiuser concurrency guarantees. A network service would require a separate architecture decision for identity and transaction isolation.\\\\n+\\\\n+The six-case experiment evaluates context engineering on a defined frozen corpus. It does not establish investment profitability, general financial forecasting performance or robustness to every future market regime. Cases include actual prices and official releases, but the selected corpus is smaller than an unrestricted research environment. Independent live judgments remain model assessments and are preserved for inspection. Deterministic facts and policy results do not rely on those judgments.\\\\n+\\\\n+The baseline tag was newly released and is supported here by the recorded regression run. Future upstream or provider changes can invalidate adapter assumptions and require another full test cycle. Offline replay establishes reconstruction of captured state, while a controlled live rerun can produce a different recommendation. Any unavailable external branch-protection capability is described in the GitHub results rather than hidden behind local checks.\\\\n+\\\\n+The project evidence reflects the authorized evaluation workflow under leo. It does not claim the participation of a real three-person student team or human approvals that did not occur. The course's transcript wording varies between one full raw session and five annotated sessions; the submission retains the actual complete sessions and maps their stages without fabricating extra conversations. The exact deployment and experimental outcomes are reported with their saved evidence.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 11. Reflection: leo, evaluation identifier leo\\\\n+\\\\n+The most important lesson from this project was that useful supervision concentrates on the meaning of a contract. The coding agent quickly produced a large runnable slice, and the first successful test run created a natural temptation to treat the implementation as finished. Reading the actual policy showed why that would have been premature. A limit on one purchase looked similar to a limit on the resulting holding, yet the two rules permit different portfolio states. The same issue appeared in approval binding: identifying the symbol and price did not identify the quantity the operator had accepted. Those findings changed my review practice. I looked for a short example that separates the intended behavior from the plausible wrong implementation, then supplied that example to OpenCode. I also learned to distinguish an optimization mechanism from an optimization result. Deduplicating a memory string was valid code, but fresh research cases had little memory to compress. The experiment needed changes at the actual per-agent input boundary and actual provider usage before it could support a cost claim. Keeping the real upstream graph made that reasoning more demanding and more useful because it prevented the project from winning by silently removing work. The evidence package improved my ability to review both kinds of result. It connected a report to its inputs and calls, while the ledger record connected a state change to a concrete approval and policy decision. Parallel work helped when each owner had a bounded responsibility: application code, CI, documentation and the recorded demonstration could progress without rewriting one another's files. Ending an overgrown code session after a useful milestone was another practical improvement. A fresh focused prompt preserved momentum better than asking the same session to keep polishing indefinitely. I would carry these habits into future projects: define observable acceptance examples first, inspect the real interface before instructing an agent, preserve failed evidence, and keep claims proportional to the operation that was actually performed. The project strengthened my understanding that engineering leadership with a coding agent is an active design and review task. It requires choosing the next concrete uncertainty to resolve and maintaining the correspondence between requirements, executable behavior and evidence.\\\\n+\\\\n+## 12. The concrete plan and tests were approved at 12:05:17.791955 UTC before OpenCode's first implementation event at 12:06:32.695 UTC.\\\\n+\\\\n+## Context and alternatives\\\\n+\\\\n+TradingAgents v0.4.0 already provides multi-agent research, structured decisions, date-aware memory, checkpointing and price validation. The missing product workflow is portable evidence followed by explicit approval and paper execution. A complete graph rewrite would discard tested domain behavior and make the optimization baseline incomparable. Editing every upstream prompt and tool would distribute application-specific policy across many owners. A narrow application extension keeps the experimental boundary visible.\\\\n+\\\\n+Candidate A modifies the entire graph and shared vendors. Candidate B subclasses/composes the existing graph and implements policy outside it. Candidate C builds a small new agent demo. The evaluation table selects B because it preserves genuine AI integration while keeping deterministic authority isolated. The original graph's full selected role sequence is retained in both experimental arms.\\\\n+\\\\n+## Context layers and assembly\\\\n+\\\\n+Layer1 identifies the instrument and analysis cutoff. Layer2 states standing constraints: use available evidence, retain source identity, distinguish unknown facts and keep execution advisory. Layer3 supplies frozen market/history/news knowledge. Layer4 holds current discussion and retrieved past context. Layer5 preserves resumable structured state. Layer6 gives the current agent task and expected output.\\\\n+\\\\n+The assembly order is eligibility filtering, duplicate removal in compact mode, prioritization, budget accounting, compaction and final constraint reinjection. Baseline preserves original substantive prompt input. Compact can remove repeated paragraphs or shorten older discussion, while retaining symbol, date, price evidence, source IDs and current task. It also requests concise role output to reduce repeated prose passed to later agents. Fresh six-case runs have little past memory, so compact must apply to actual per-agent messages; changing only a memory string would leave the dominant token cost unchanged.\\\\n+\\\\n+The call budget is configured for the experiment. Per-call maximum output bounds use the provider's existing max_tokens contract. Character estimates may guide context assembly but never replace provider-reported token usage. The model adapter checks before starting a request; a structured-output retry cannot create an extra request after the budget is exhausted. Critical constraints are re-injected after compaction. Factual quality is evaluated independently of brevity.\\\\n+\\\\n+## Consequences and reopening conditions\\\\n+\\\\n+Evidence packs contain prompts and responses and are larger than ordinary reports. Replay is fast because it reconstructs captured state; controlled reruns call the model and remain stochastic. The frozen provider must answer valid parameter variations from data, because an exact tool-transcript lookup would bias the comparison when compact changes tool arguments.\\\\n+\\\\n+The approval boundary stays outside all model tools. The extension retains responsibility for current-ledger checks even if upstream research changes. Reopen this ADR if an upstream public interface cannot expose a material external read, if multiuser concurrency is added, or if compact cannot satisfy factual constraints without discarding agent roles. Its raw record includes implementation attempts, test failures and corrections. The coordinating review examined business contracts instead of relying entirely on the agent's success statement. A decision can authorize a plan, but it cannot declare an unrun test successful. An ADR can select an architecture, but it cannot establish measured token savings. A network service would require a separate architecture decision for identity and transaction isolation.\n \n The six-case experiment evaluates context engineering on a defined frozen corpus. Reflection: leo, evaluation identifier leo\n \n The most important lesson from this project was that useful supervision concentrates on the meaning of a contract. The coding agent quickly produced a large runnable slice, and the first successful test run created a natural temptation to treat the implementation as finished. Reading the actual policy showed why that would have been premature. A limit on one purchase looked similar to a limit on the resulting holding, yet the two rules permit different portfolio states. The same issue appeared in approval binding: identifying the symbol and price did not identify the quantity the operator had accepted. Those findings changed my review practice. I looked for a short example that separates the intended behavior from the plausible wrong implementation, then supplied that example to OpenCode. I also learned to distinguish an optimization mechanism from an optimization result. Deduplicating a memory string was valid code, but fresh research cases had little memory to compress. The experiment needed changes at the actual per-agent input boundary and actual provider usage before it could support a cost claim. Keeping the real upstream graph made that reasoning more demanding and more useful because it prevented the project from winning by silently removing work. The evidence package improved my ability to review both kinds of result. It connected a report to its inputs and calls, while the ledger record connected a state change to a concrete approval and policy decision. Parallel work helped when each owner had a bounded responsibility: application code, CI, documentation and the recorded demonstration could progress without rewriting one another's files. Ending an overgrown code session after a useful milestone was another practical improvement. A fresh focused prompt preserved momentum better than asking the same session to keep polishing indefinitely. I would carry these habits into future projects: define observable acceptance examples first, inspect the real interface before instructing an agent, preserve failed evidence, and keep claims proportional to the operation that was actually performed. The project strengthened my understanding that engineering leadership with a coding agent is an active design and review task. set RESEARCH_DESK_LIVE_TESTS=1 and DEEPSEEK_API_KEY\",\n+)\n+\n+\n+def _live_out(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:\n+    explicit = os.environ.get(\"RESEARCH_DESK_LIVE_OUT\")\n+    if explicit:\n+        d = Path(explicit)\n+        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n+        return d\n+    return tmp_path\n+\n+\n+def test_one_frozen_aapl_baseline(tmp_path):\n+    if \"DEEPSEEK_API_KEY\" not in os.environ:\n+        pytest.skip(\"DEEPSEEK_API_KEY not set; skipping live call\")\n+\n+    from research_desk.eval.live import run_evaluate_case\n+\n+    out = _live_out(tmp_path)\n+    summary = run_evaluate_case(\"AAPL\", \"baseline\", out, max_calls=None)\n+\n+    # The actual graph must have completed (a failed setup is never 'completed').\n+    assert summary[\"outcome\"] == \"completed\", summary\n+\n+    # The completed pack must import cleanly and carry real material.\n+    pack = EvidencePackIO().import_pack(Path(summary[\"run_dir\"]))\n+    assert pack.manifest.outcome == \"completed\"\n+    assert pack.manifest.ticker == \"AAPL\"\n+    assert pack.manifest.context_mode == \"baseline\"\n+    # Real numeric usage from the provider (not a fabricated placeholder).\n+    assert pack.usage.calls > 0\n+    assert pack.usage.total_tokens > 0\n+    assert pack.usage.output_tokens > 0\n+    # A completed run must carry a final decision.\n+    assert pack.final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\"), \"completed run lacks a final decision\"\n",

def _augmented_pack(aapl_pack: EvidencePack) -> EvidencePack:
    """aapl_buy_complete with real messages, numeric usage and a credential field.

    ``final_state`` gains a LangChain message list (HumanMessage/AIMessage with

    pack = aapl_pack.model_copy(deep=True)

    ]

+              "content": """"Permission configuration check (part of Gate 2).

Validates the effective OpenCode permission configuration and the reviewable
``.opencode/permissions.jsonc`` manifest agree, the required rule files are
loaded, and each concrete role (plan / build / verify) cannot step outside its
approved boundary.

OpenCode does not load ``permissions.jsonc``; it is only a reviewable
projection. The authoritative file is the effective root ``opencode.json``
(candidate becomes authoritative only after installation). This check therefore
reads the effective config and verifies the manifest against it.

Evaluation model
----------------
- Path tools (read / edit / glob / grep / bash / task / skill) can carry
  granular object rules. A rule object maps a glob pattern to an action
  (allow / ask / deny); the last matching pattern wins, and agent rules are
  evaluated after global rules so they take precedence.
- Wildcards follow OpenCode's documented simple semantics: ``*`` matches zero
  or more of any character, ``?`` matches exactly one, everything else is
  literal.

The boundary assertions are the enforcement: if a protected path ever resolves
to a non-deny ``edit`` (or a forbidden path resolves to allow), the check
reports it, so a misconfigured build role that can edit approvals or a verify
role that can edit application code is detected.

Schema validation is required. The vendored official schema
``.opencode/config-schema.json`` is validated first; both the effective config
and the manifest are then validated against the real official schema (no subset
or network-fetched schema), and their projection agreement is checked. Default
mode (no ``--config``) inspects the actually installed root config and fails
until the approved candidate is installed. ``--config PATH`` enables the
focused candidate check used during preparation.

This is coding-tool enforcement, not an OS sandbox: it does not claim to stop
arbitrary malicious code inside approved tests.

def _wildcard_to_regex(pattern: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
    """Convert OpenCode's simple wildcard pattern to a compiled regex.

    ``*`` -> zero or more of any character; ``?`` -> exactly one character;
    all other characters match literally.
    """
    out: list[str] = []
    for ch in pattern:
        if ch == "*":
            out.append(".*")
        elif ch == "?":
            out.append(".")
        else:
            out.append(re.escape(ch))
    return re.compile("".join(out))


def _resolve(tool_rules: dict[str, str], target: str) -> str | None:
    """Resolve the effective action for ``target`` under object rules.

    The last matching pattern wins, per OpenCode's documented semantics.
    """
    action: str | None = None
    for pattern, value in tool_rules.items():
        if value not in ("allow", "ask", "deny"):
            continue
        if _wildcard_to_regex(pattern).fullmatch(target):
            action = value
    return action


def _effective_rules(config: dict, role: str, tool: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Merge global + agent rules for ``role``/``tool``, agent rules last.

    Evaluating agent rules after global rules gives them precedence and
    preserves last-matching-wins within each source.
    """
    merged: dict[str, str] = {}
    global_rules = (config.get("permission") or {}).get(tool)
    agent_rules = (
        (config.get("agent") or {}).get(role, {}).get("permission", {}).get(tool)
    )
    for rules in (global_rules, agent_rules):
        if isinstance(rules, dict):
            merged.update(rules)
    return merged


def _expect_deny(config: dict, role: str, tool: str, paths: tuple[str, ...],
                 why: str, failures: list[str]) -> None:
    for target in paths:
        action = _resolve(_effective_rules(config, role, tool), target)
        if action != "deny":
            failures.append(
                f"{role} role must NOT be able to {tool} {target} "
                f"({why}); resolved action is {action!r}"
            )


def _expect_allow(config: dict, role: str, tool: str, paths: tuple[str, ...],
                  why: str, failures: list[str]) -> None:
    for target in paths:
        action = _resolve(_effective_rules(config, role, tool), target)
        if action != "allow":
            failures.append(
                f"{role} role must be able to {tool} {target} "
                f"({why}); resolved action is {action!r}"
            )


def _load_json(path: Path) -> dict | None:
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid JSON in {path}: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"{path} must contain a JSON object")
    return data


def _load_schema(path: Path, failures: list[str]) -> dict | None:
    if not path.exists():
        failures.append(f"official schema not found at {path}; schema validation is required")
        return None
    try:
        import jsonschema  # required: the vendored schema check is part of Gate 2
    except ImportError:
        failures.append("jsonschema is not installed; schema validation is required")
        return None
    try:
        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
        failures.append(f"invalid official schema at {path}: {exc}")
        return None


def _check_schema(instance: dict, name: str, schema_path: Path, failures: list[str]) -> None:
    schema = _load_schema(schema_path, failures)
    if schema is None:
        return
    import jsonschema  # already confirmed available by _load_schema

    validator = jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema)
    for error in sorted(validator.iter_errors(instance), key=lambda e: list(e.path)):
        failures.append(f"{name} does not match the official OpenCode schema: {error.message}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Permission configuration check.")
    parser.add_argument("--root", default=None, help="Repository root (defaults to project root).")
    parser.add_argument("--config", default=None,
                        help="Effective config file to inspect (default: <root>/opencode.json).")
    parser.add_argument("--schema", default=None,
                        help="Official OpenCode config schema (default: <root>/.opencode/config-schema.json).")
    parser.add_argument("--manifest", default=None,
                        help="Reviewable permission manifest (default: <root>/.opencode/permissions.jsonc).")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    root = (
        Path(args.root).resolve()
        if args.root
        else Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    )

    config_path = Path(args.config).resolve() if args.config else root / "opencode.json"
    schema_path = (
        Path(args.schema).resolve()
        if args.schema
        else root / ".opencode" / "config-schema.json"
    )
    manifest_path = (
        Path(args.manifest).resolve()
        if args.manifest
        else root / ".opencode" / "permissions.jsonc"
    )

    checks: list[str] = []
    failures: list[str] = []

    try:
        config = _load_json(config_path)
        manifest = _load_json(manifest_path)
    except ValueError as exc:
        failures.append(str(exc))
        return _report(checks, failures)

    if config is None:
        failures.append(f"missing effective config: {config_path}")
    if manifest is None:
        failures.append(f"missing permission manifest: {manifest_path}")
    if failures:
        return _report(checks, failures)

    checks.append(f"read effective config {config_path}")
    checks.append(f"read manifest {manifest_path}")
    checks.append(f"official schema {schema_path}")

    # Required schema validation of BOTH the config and the manifest.
    _check_schema(config, "effective config", schema_path, failures)
    _check_schema(manifest, "manifest", schema_path, failures)

    # Required rule files must be loaded through the instructions array.
    instructions = config.get("instructions")
    if not isinstance(instructions, list):
        failures.append("config must declare an instructions array")
    else:
        for rule in RULE_FILES:
            if rule not in instructions:
                failures.append(f"required rule file is not loaded via instructions: {rule}")
    checks.append(
        "instructions rules present: "
        + f"{[r for r in RULE_FILES if r in (instructions or [])]}"
    )

    # Manifest is a projection using only $schema / permission / agent.
    unknown_keys = [k for k in manifest if k not in MANIFEST_KEYS]
    if unknown_keys:
        failures.append(f"manifest carries unsupported keys: {sorted(unknown_keys)}")
    for key in REQUIRED_MANIFEST_KEYS:
        if key not in manifest:
            failures.append(f"manifest missing required projection key: {key}")

    # Agreement: manifest projection must equal the effective global permission
    # and role definitions.
    if manifest.get("permission") != config.get("permission"):
        failures.append("manifest permission projection does not match the effective config")
    if manifest.get("agent") != config.get("agent"):
        failures.append("manifest agent projection does not match the effective config")
    checks.append("manifest agrees with effective permission and agent definitions")

    # Default policy must be no access until granted: global and bash catch-alls
    # must be deny, and network/delegation/external tools must be denied.
    global_permission = config.get("permission") or {}
    if global_permission.get("*") != "deny":
        failures.append("global permission default must be deny (no access until granted)")
    bash_default = global_permission.get("bash")
    if isinstance(bash_default, dict) and bash_default.get("*") != "deny":
        failures.append("global bash default must be deny")
    for tool in ("webfetch", "websearch", "task", "external_directory"):
        if global_permission.get(tool) != "deny":
            failures.append(f"global {tool} must be denied")

    # Concrete role boundaries (edit tool is the write authority).
    _expect_deny(config, "build", "edit", BUILD_PROTECTED_EDIT,
                 "protected rule/approval/frozen-upstream/safety path", failures)
    _expect_allow(config, "build", "edit", BUILD_ALLOWED_EDIT,
                  "approved application/test/CI path", failures)
    _expect_deny(config, "verify", "edit", VERIFY_FORBIDDEN_EDIT,
                 "verify must not edit source or weaken tests", failures)
    _expect_allow(config, "verify", "edit", VERIFY_ALLOWED_EDIT,
                  "verification output only", failures)
    _expect_deny(config, "plan", "edit", PLAN_FORBIDDEN_EDIT,
                 "plan must not modify implementation or approve work", failures)
    _expect_allow(config, "plan", "edit", PLAN_ALLOWED_EDIT,
                  "proposed plan documents only", failures)

    # A build role must never bypass file-tool write restrictions through bash.
    if _resolve(_effective_rules(config, "build", "bash"), "python -c 1") == "allow":
        failures.append("build role must not run arbitrary python via bash")
    if _resolve(_effective_rules(config, "build", "bash"), "bash -c 1") == "allow":
        failures.append("build role must not run nested shell via bash")
    # Verify must not run arbitrary python or shell interpreters.
    if _resolve(_effective_rules(config, "verify", "bash"), "python -c 1") == "allow":
        failures.append("verify role must not run arbitrary python via bash")
    if _resolve(_effective_rules(config, "verify", "bash"), "bash -c 1") == "allow":
        failures.append("verify role must not run a shell interpreter via bash")
    # No role may delegate to a subagent or reach the network in this workflow.
    for role in ("plan", "build", "verify"):
        for tool, why in (("task", "subagent delegation"), ("webfetch", "network fetch"),
                          ("websearch", "web search")):
            if config.get("agent", {}).get(role, {}).get("permission", {}).get(tool) == "allow":
                failures.append(f"{role} role must not allow {tool} ({why})")

    return _report(checks, failures)


def _report(checks: list[str], failures: list[str]) -> int:
    for line in checks:
        print(line)
    print("RESULT: FAIL" if failures else "RESULT: PASS")
    if failures:
        print("FAILURES:")
        for f in failures:
            print(f"- {f}")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1: # Permission model
2: 
3: The principle is no access until a role needs a path. The machine-readable permissions and effective OpenCode configuration must agree; a file named permissions.jsonc alone is not enforcement. The host keeps credentials outside agent-readable files and injects only the application's runtime environment.
4: 
5: | Role | Read | Write | Forbidden |
6: |---|---|---|---|
7: | Plan | AGENTS, Prompt, docs, public upstream source, src/test declarations | proposed plan documents | Application implementation, approvals, secrets |
8: | Build | Approved requirements/architecture/tests, src, test, pyproject | src/research_desk, approved test files, scoped package metadata | Human-owned rules/approval decisions, global config, upstream replacement |
9: | Verify | Source, tests, requirements, frozen fixtures, run evidence | verification outputs and proposed test changes | Granting approval, weakening requirements, editing source to force a result |
10: | Release | Final artifacts and local git state | package, workflow evidence, authorized private remote | Publishing credentials, public release, real orders |
11: | leo | All project decisions and review evidence | Plans, ADRs, rules, concrete stage approvals | Falsifying raw sessions or measured results |
12: 
13: Runtime authority is separate from coding-agent permissions. The graph has market/news tools and model access. It has no review, execute or ledger tool. The local operator commands own approval and execution. This is a single-user workstation boundary, not a claim of production identity assurance.
14: 
15: Safety-relevant paths include policy.py, review.py, storage.py, config.py, model contracts, permission configuration and rule files. Changes need a reviewed ADR plus a corresponding approval record. Current fixes to total holdings, valid sells and exact approval binding are covered by ADR-002 and the approved AT-04/05 semantics.

1: """Gate 2: lint, types, dependencies and the deterministic authority boundary.
2: 
3: Runs ``ruff check .`` over the repository, a meaningful mypy check over the new
4: ``src/research_desk`` package (``--follow-imports=skip`` so the untouched
5: upstream package is not silently made part of the new type contract), and
6: ``python -m pip check`` for dependency consistency. It then scans the policy /
7: review / storage / graph-adapter modules for the structural authority boundary:
8: ``review`` and ``policy`` must never import an LLM (including direct provider
9: modules and upstream LLM factories), and the graph must never import a function
10: that grants approval or mutates the ledger.
11: 
12: Genuine application lint/type findings are reported with file:line and the gate
13: fails; this implementation does not own application source, so findings are
14: surfaced to the supervisor rather than suppressed.
15: 
16: In PR mode, a change on a safety-relevant path must carry, in the same diff, a
17: changed ADR that references the changed owner/path AND a changed concrete
18: approval record carrying the real APPROVED marker and owner.
19: """
20: 
21: from __future__ import annotations
22: 
23: import argparse
24: import ast
25: import re
26: from pathlib import Path
27: 
28: import yaml
29: from _gate_lib import add_change_args, changed_files, fail, resolve_root, run, tool_path
30: 
31: # Modules that own deterministic authority and therefore must not touch an LLM.
32: NO_LLM_MODULES = ("policy", "review")
33: # Top-level LLM providers / frameworks the authority owners must not import.
34: LLM_PROVIDER_PREFIXES = (
35:     "langchain",
36:     "openai",
37:     "anthropic",
38:     "google",
39:     "google_genai",
40:     "zhipu",
41:     "zhipuai",
42:     "minimax",
43:     "openrouter",
44:     "dashscope",
45:     "dashscopen",
46:     "bedrock",
47:     "boto3",
48: )
49: # Upstream LLM factory names (checked by original imported name, not only alias).
50: LLM_FACTORY_NAMES = {"create_llm_client", "create_llm"}
51: # Functions that grant approval or mutate the ledger; the graph must not import them.
52: LEDGER_AUTHORITY_NAMES = {
53:     "approve",
54:     "execute",
55:     "apply_transaction",
56:     "ResearchDeskStore",
57:     "save_proposal",
58: }
59: # Safety-relevant paths (deterministic authority, persistent models, permission
60: # and rule/config files as declared by permission-model.md).
61: SAFETY_PATHS = (
62:     "src/research_desk/policy.py",
63:     "src/research_desk/review.py",
64:     "src/research_desk/storage.py",
65:     "src/research_desk/config.py",
66:     "src/research_desk/models.py",
67:     ".agent/rules.md",
68:     ".opencode/rules.md",
69:     ".opencode/permissions.jsonc",
70:     "opencode.json",
71: )
72: APPROVAL_DOC = "docs/process/test-approval.yaml"
73: ADR_PREFIX = "docs/architecture/adr/"
74: APPROVER = "leo"
75: 
76: 
77: def _import_names(tree: ast.Module) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
78:     """Return (top-level module names, imported original member names).
79: 
80:     Uses the *original* imported names (``alias.name``) rather than only
81:     aliases, so ``from x import approve as y`` is still detected.
82:     """
83:     modules: list[str] = []
84:     members: list[str] = []
85:     for node in ast.walk(tree):
86:         if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
87:             modules.extend(alias.name for alias in node.names)
88:         elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
89:             if node.module:
90:                 modules.append(node.module)
91:             members.extend(alias.name for alias in node.names)
92:     return modules, members

Runs ``ruff check .`` over the repository, a meaningful mypy check over the new
``src/research_desk`` package (``--follow-imports=skip`` so the untouched
